tasks.title: Explain the agentic loop and pick the right extension for a recurring need
knowledge: The loop has three blended phases (gather context, take action, verify results), powered by a model that reasons and tools that act.

Claude Code is the agentic harness: it supplies tools, context management, permission gating and the loop; a turn runs from your message until Claude finishes, with any number of tool calls in between.
Each extension has a trigger and a context cost: CLAUDE.md always loaded, skills on demand, MCP tool names deferred, subagents isolated, hooks zero unless they return output.
Instructions (CLAUDE.md, output styles, skills) are guidance Claude interprets; hooks and permission rules are enforcement.

autoUpdatesChannel is "latest" (default) or "stable" (about a week old); minimumVersion sets a floor.
DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER stops only the background check; DISABLE_UPDATES blocks every update path.
Credential precedence runs from cloud-provider variables down to the /login subscription, so an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment wins over a subscription once approved.

tasks.title: Predict how Claude's built-in tools behave and reference them in configuration

Permission rules use ToolName(specifier), e.g. Bash(npm run *), Edit(/src/**), WebFetch(domain:example.com); hook matchers use bare names.
Edit is exact string replacement that needs a prior read, an exact match and a unique old_string (or replace_all); Write overwrites a whole file.
Bash runs each command in a separate process: cwd carries over inside the project, environment variables do not.

Shortcuts live in ~/.claude/keybindings.json (opened with /keybindings) as context blocks mapping keystrokes to actions.
A statusLine setting of type "command" runs a script that receives session JSON on stdin and prints the status line.

concepts.title: The agentic loop: gather context, act, verify
concepts.titleEs: El loop agéntico: reunir contexto, actuar, verificar
concepts.summary: Claude works in three blended phases (gather context -> take action -> verify results), repeating until done; the model reasons and the tools act, and Claude Code is the harness that provides tools, context management and permission gating. A turn runs from your message until Claude finishes responding, with any number of tool calls in between, and each tool result feeds the next decision.

concepts.title: Which extension fits which recurring need
concepts.titleEs: Qué extensión corresponde a cada necesidad recurrente
concepts.summary: Map the trigger to the feature: a convention Claude gets wrong twice goes in CLAUDE.md, a prompt you retype becomes a skill, data Claude cannot see needs an MCP server, a side task that floods context goes to a subagent, something that must happen every time is a hook, and a second repo needing the same setup gets a plugin. Context cost differs: CLAUDE.md loads fully every request, skill descriptions load at start and bodies on use, MCP loads tool names with schemas deferred, subagents use a separate window, hooks cost nothing unless they return output.

concepts.title: Guidance (CLAUDE.md, skills) vs enforcement (hooks, permissions)
concepts.titleEs: Guía (CLAUDE.md, skills) vs garantía (hooks, permisos)
concepts.summary: An instruction like "never edit .env" in CLAUDE.md, an output style or a skill is a request Claude interprets; a PreToolUse hook or a permission deny rule is enforcement that holds regardless of what Claude decides. Use CLAUDE.md for "we do it this way here" and hooks or permissions for security boundaries and anything that must never happen.

concepts.title: Install methods, auto-updates and release channels
concepts.titleEs: Métodos de instalación, auto-updates y canales
concepts.summary: The native installer (curl install.sh / irm install.ps1) puts claude at ~/.local/bin and auto-updates in the background, applied on next start; Homebrew, WinGet, apt, dnf and apk need manual upgrades. In settings.json, autoUpdatesChannel is "latest" (default) or "stable" (about a week old), minimumVersion sets a floor, env DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER="1" stops only the background check (claude update still works) while DISABLE_UPDATES blocks all update paths; "command not found" after install means ~/.local/bin is not on PATH.

concepts.title: Which credential wins: API key, OAuth token or subscription
concepts.titleEs: Qué credencial gana: API key, token OAuth o suscripción
concepts.summary: Order: cloud provider (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / _VERTEX / _FOUNDRY) > ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (bearer, for gateways) > ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (X-Api-Key) > apiKeyHelper script > CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN > Anthropic profiles > /login subscription. A leftover ANTHROPIC_API_KEY overrides your subscription once approved (unset it and check /status); for CI without a browser, run claude setup-token to get a one-year token and export it as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

concepts.title: Tool names and the ToolName(specifier) rule format
concepts.titleEs: Nombres de herramientas y el formato ToolName(especificador)
concepts.summary: Built-in tool names (Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, Agent, Skill, ...) are the exact strings used in permissions.allow/deny, --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, a skill's allowed-tools and a subagent's tools; rules use ToolName(specifier) such as Bash(npm run *), Read(~/secrets/**), Edit(/src/**), WebFetch(domain:example.com), while hook matchers take bare case-sensitive names like "Edit|Write". On macOS, Linux and WSL, Glob and Grep are absent by default and searches run as Bash find/grep; on Windows without Git for Windows, PowerShell is the shell tool.

concepts.title: Edit vs Write: exact replacement vs full overwrite
concepts.titleEs: Edit vs Write: reemplazo exacto vs sobrescritura completa
concepts.summary: Edit replaces an exact old_string with new_string (no regex or fuzzy match) and needs three checks: the file was read this conversation, old_string matches exactly including whitespace, and it appears exactly once unless replace_all is true. Write creates or overwrites a whole file (never appends) and is used for new files; for partial changes Claude uses Edit. Read returns numbered lines, pages large files with a PARTIAL view notice, and handles images, PDFs (pages ranges) and notebooks but not directories.

concepts.title: What persists between Bash commands
concepts.titleEs: Qué persiste entre comandos de Bash
concepts.summary: Each Bash command runs in a separate process: a cd inside the project (or an --add-dir directory) carries over, but exported environment variables do not, so persist them with CLAUDE_ENV_FILE or a SessionStart hook and activate virtualenvs before launching. Default timeout is 2 minutes (BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS) with a 10-minute ceiling (BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS); long processes run with run_in_background and are managed with /tasks, and a command that hits its timeout moves to the background.

concepts.title: Esc to interrupt vs Enter to queue a correction
concepts.titleEs: Esc para interrumpir vs Enter para encolar una corrección
concepts.summary: Esc stops the current response or tool call and waits for you; typing and pressing Enter while Claude works queues the message, which Claude reads as soon as the running tool calls finish, within the same turn. Ctrl+Enter sends the queue now, Up takes queued text back, Esc Esc clears a draft or opens rewind on an empty input, Ctrl+B backgrounds running commands, Ctrl+O toggles the transcript viewer, Shift+Tab cycles permission modes and Ctrl+G opens the prompt in your editor.

concepts.title: Input prefixes: /, !, @ and multiline
concepts.titleEs: Prefijos de entrada: /, !, @ y multilínea
concepts.summary: / starts a command or skill, @ autocompletes a file path so Claude reads it, and ! enters shell mode: the command runs directly without Claude approving it, its output is added to context and Claude responds to it (set respondToBashCommands to false to only add the output). Newlines: \ + Enter or Ctrl+J work everywhere, Shift+Enter natively in many terminals (/terminal-setup installs it for VS Code and others).

concepts.title: Customize shortcuts and the status line
concepts.titleEs: Personalizar atajos y la status line
concepts.summary: /keybindings opens ~/.claude/keybindings.json: a bindings array of blocks with a context (Global, Chat, Confirmation, ...) and a map of keystrokes to actions, where null unbinds; changes apply without restart. A status line is set in settings as "statusLine": {"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/statusline.sh", "padding", "refreshInterval"}; the script gets session JSON on stdin and prints lines to stdout, costs no tokens, and /statusline can generate it. /tui fullscreen switches to the flicker-free renderer.

concepts.title: /init, /config, /diff, /add-dir and /export
concepts.titleEs: /init, /config, /diff, /add-dir y /export
concepts.summary: /init generates a starter CLAUDE.md for the project; /config opens the Settings interface or sets keys directly (/config model=sonnet, /config theme=dark), also in -p mode; /diff reviews working-tree changes including Claude's edits; /add-dir <path> grants file access to another directory for the session but most of its .claude/ configuration is not discovered; /export [filename] saves the conversation as plain text.

concepts.title: /btw: a side question with no tools and no history
concepts.titleEs: /btw: una pregunta lateral sin herramientas ni historial
concepts.summary: /btw <question> answers from what is already in context (messages, tool results), even while Claude is working, without interrupting the turn and without adding to the conversation history; it has no tool access, so it cannot read files or run commands. Use /btw for what the session already knows, a subagent to find out something new; press f in the overlay to fork the question into a background subagent with tools.

concepts.title: Rewind menu: restore code, conversation or summarize
concepts.titleEs: Menú de rewind: restaurar código, conversación o resumir
concepts.summary: Every prompt that starts a turn creates a checkpoint (the 100 most recent keep file snapshots, saved with the session so /rewind works after resume, swept after about 30 days per cleanupPeriodDays). /rewind or Esc Esc on an empty input lists your prompts; pick one and choose Restore code and conversation, Restore conversation (keep code), Restore code (keep conversation), Summarize from here, Summarize up to here, or Never mind; summarizing frees context without touching files.

concepts.title: What rewind cannot undo
concepts.titleEs: Lo que el rewind no puede deshacer
concepts.summary: Checkpoints track only edits made by Claude's file-editing tools in this session: changes made through Bash (rm, mv, cp), edits by background subagents, manual or other-session edits, symlinked and hard-linked files, and remote effects (databases, APIs, deployments) are not restored. Messages queued mid-turn get no checkpoint of their own; use git for anything rewind misses, and permissions to guard remote actions.

concepts.title: Model aliases and where the model choice comes from
concepts.titleEs: Alias de modelo y de dónde sale la elección
concepts.summary: Aliases sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, best, sonnet[1m], opus[1m] resolve to the recommended version per provider (pin with a full name like claude-opus-5-5); opusplan uses Opus in plan mode and Sonnet for execution. Priority: /model in session > claude --model > ANTHROPIC_MODEL > "model" in settings > ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL; /model saves the default while pressing s in the picker switches this session only. The advisor (/advisor, advisorModel, --advisor) lets Claude consult a stronger model at decision points instead of switching the main model.

concepts.title: Effort levels, ultrathink and fast mode
concepts.titleEs: Niveles de esfuerzo, ultrathink y fast mode
concepts.summary: Effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) controls how much the model reasons; resolution order is explicit choice (CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, --effort, /effort) > saved settings > model default (high, but medium on Opus 5.5), and max applies to the current session only. Writing ultrathink in a prompt asks for deeper reasoning on that one turn without changing the setting. Fast mode (/fast or "fastMode": true) is the same Opus model up to 2.5x faster at a higher per-token price, unlike lower effort, which trades quality for speed.

concepts.title: Output styles: how Claude responds
concepts.titleEs: Estilos de salida: cómo responde Claude
concepts.summary: Built-in styles are Default, Proactive, Concise, Explanatory (Insight blocks) and Learning (leaves TODO(human) for you); switch with /output-style <style> or /config, which saves "outputStyle" (case-sensitive) to .claude/settings.local.json. A custom style is a Markdown file in ~/.claude/output-styles or .claude/output-styles with frontmatter name, description and keep-coding-instructions (default false drops the software-engineering instructions); it is sent with every request and is guidance, not enforcement, while CLAUDE.md holds what Claude should know about the project.

concepts.title: Give Claude a way to verify its work
concepts.titleEs: Darle a Claude una forma de verificar su trabajo
concepts.summary: Without a runnable check Claude stops when work looks done and you become the verification loop; give it tests, a build exit code, a linter or a screenshot to compare, and ask for evidence rather than claims. Gate the stop with increasing rigor: in the prompt, across the session with a /goal condition, deterministically with a Stop hook, or by a second opinion from a verification subagent or workflow.

concepts.title: Explore, plan, implement, commit
concepts.titleEs: Explorar, planificar, implementar, commitear
concepts.summary: The recommended order is explore (plan mode via Shift+Tab or claude --permission-mode plan, reading without edits) -> plan (ask for a plan, edit it with Ctrl+G) -> implement (approve the plan, verify against it) -> commit (message and PR). Skip planning when you could describe the diff in one sentence; feed context with @file references, pasted images, URLs or piped input like cat error.log | claude.

concepts.title: Common session failure patterns and their fixes
concepts.titleEs: Patrones de fallo comunes en una sesión y su arreglo
concepts.summary: Kitchen-sink session with unrelated tasks -> /clear between tasks; two failed corrections -> /clear and write a better first prompt; over-specified CLAUDE.md -> prune or turn rules into hooks; plausible code with missed edge cases -> always provide verification; unscoped "investigate" filling context -> scope it or delegate to a subagent.

concepts.title: Inspect what loaded: /context, /doctor, /status, /debug
concepts.titleEs: Inspeccionar qué cargó: /context, /doctor, /status, /debug
concepts.summary: Start with /context to see whether CLAUDE.md, rules, skills and MCP tools loaded at all, then drill in with /memory, /skills, /hooks, /mcp, /permissions and /status (active settings sources, managed settings, login method). claude doctor in the shell prints read-only install and settings diagnostics; /doctor in a session also proposes fixes and asks before applying them; /debug or claude --debug writes a log to ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt.

concepts.title: Bisect with --safe-mode, a clean CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and common causes
concepts.titleEs: Aislar el problema con --safe-mode, un CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR limpio y causas comunes
concepts.summary: claude --safe-mode disables CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP and custom commands and agents while auth, model, built-in tools and permissions work; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to an empty directory, launched outside any project, bypasses all user and project config (managed settings still apply in both). Frequent culprits: permissions or hooks placed in ~/.claude.json instead of ~/.claude/settings.json, a hook matcher written as an array or in lowercase, a skill at .claude/skills/name.md instead of .claude/skills/name/SKILL.md, and .mcp.json under .claude/ instead of the repo root.

concepts.title: What loads into context before your first prompt
concepts.titleEs: Qué se carga en el contexto antes de tu primer prompt
concepts.summary: In the docs' timeline the startup context loads in this order: system prompt, auto memory (first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md), environment info (cwd, platform, git), MCP tool names (schemas deferred via tool search), one-line skill descriptions (skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` are left out), ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, then project CLAUDE.md. While Claude works, file reads, path-scoped rules and hook `additionalContext` are appended; the terminal shows a one-liner but the full content costs context, and `!command` output enters context as part of your message.

concepts.title: /context: see what is consuming the window
concepts.titleEs: /context: ver qué está consumiendo la ventana
concepts.summary: Run `/context` for a live colored grid of context usage by category with optimization suggestions (context-heavy tools, memory bloat, capacity warnings) and a Memory files list confirming which CLAUDE.md, rules and auto memory files loaded; `/context all` expands the per-item breakdown. It answers 'what is in my window', not 'what did it cost' (that is /usage).

concepts.title: /clear: start fresh between unrelated tasks
concepts.titleEs: /clear: empezar de cero entre tareas no relacionadas
concepts.summary: `/clear` (aliases `/reset`, `/new`) starts a new conversation with empty context; the previous one is saved and resumable with `/resume`, and `/clear <name>` labels it in the picker. Use it when switching to unrelated work or after correcting Claude twice on the same issue (then re-prompt with what you learned); unlike /compact it costs nothing. For a side question that should never enter history, use `/btw` instead.

concepts.title: /compact and auto-compaction: summarize to free space
concepts.titleEs: /compact y la autocompactación: resumir para liberar espacio
concepts.summary: `/compact [instructions]` replaces the conversation with a structured summary, optionally focused (`/compact focus on the auth bug fix`); a `# Compact instructions` section in project CLAUDE.md steers every compaction. Auto-compaction runs as you approach the limit, and `/autocompact 500k` sets how full the window gets first (`auto` restores the model default). To condense only part, use `/rewind` (or Esc Esc) → Summarize from here / Summarize up to here. Compacting reads the whole conversation, so it is itself a large request.

concepts.title: What survives compaction and what is lost
concepts.titleEs: Qué sobrevive a la compactación y qué se pierde
concepts.summary: After compaction: system prompt and output style still apply; project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules, auto memory and the plan-mode plan file are re-injected from disk; up to five recently modified files are re-read (files over 5,000 tokens come back as a path reference); invoked skill bodies return capped at 5,000 tokens each / 25,000 total (oldest dropped, start of SKILL.md kept); the skill description listing is not re-injected. Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md only reload when a matching file is read again, and instructions given only in chat are summarized away, so put must-keep rules in project-root CLAUDE.md or re-inject with a SessionStart hook matching `compact`.

concepts.title: The CLAUDE.md scopes and their load order
concepts.titleEs: Los scopes de CLAUDE.md y su orden de carga
concepts.summary: Load order, broadest first: managed policy (/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md, /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md; can't be excluded) → user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md → project ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md (committed) → local ./CLAUDE.local.md (gitignored). Files are concatenated, not overriding: ancestors of the cwd load at launch root-down, CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md in each directory, and subdirectory files load on demand when Claude reads there. CLAUDE.md is a user message, not enforcement: to block an action use `permissions.deny` or a PreToolUse hook.

concepts.title: @path imports and keeping CLAUDE.md lean
concepts.titleEs: Imports con @path y mantener CLAUDE.md corto
concepts.summary: `@path/to/file` imports resolve relative to the importing file, recurse up to four hops, are ignored inside backticks and code blocks, and expand at launch, so they organize but don't save context; a project import outside the working directory triggers a one-time approval dialog. Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md (a file over 4 MiB is skipped), write concrete verifiable rules, use block-level HTML comments for maintainer notes (stripped before injection), and generate a starter with `/init` (`CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1` for the interactive flow).

concepts.title: AGENTS.md: when Claude reads it instead of or with CLAUDE.md
concepts.titleEs: AGENTS.md: cuándo Claude lo lee en lugar de CLAUDE.md o junto a él
concepts.summary: By default (`claude-md-or-agents-md`) Claude reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the cwd or above (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, managed CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ don't count). Change it in /config → Project instructions: `claude-md-and-agents-md`, `claude-md` or `managed-only` (or `pluginConfigs."agents-md@builtin".options.instructionFiles` in user settings). To share one file with other tools, put `@AGENTS.md` at the top of CLAUDE.md; AGENTS.local.md and .agents/ are never read.

concepts.title: Auto memory: notes Claude writes for itself
concepts.titleEs: Auto memory: notas que Claude escribe para sí mismo
concepts.summary: Claude writes user/feedback/project/reference notes to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ (per git repo, shared across worktrees, machine-local): a MEMORY.md index whose first 200 lines or 25KB load every session, plus topic files read on demand. 'Remember X' goes to auto memory; 'add this to CLAUDE.md' goes to CLAUDE.md. Toggle it in `/memory` or with `autoMemoryEnabled: false` (or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`), relocate it with `autoMemoryDirectory` (absolute or `~/` path), and audit the plain-markdown files from `/memory`.

concepts.title: .claude/rules/ and path-scoped rules
concepts.titleEs: .claude/rules/ y reglas con alcance por ruta
concepts.summary: One-topic markdown files in .claude/rules/ (discovered recursively). The only frontmatter field is `paths` (YAML list or comma-separated globs, brace expansion allowed, e.g. `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`): without it the rule loads at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md; with it the rule loads when Claude reads a matching file, not on every tool use. User rules in ~/.claude/rules/ load before project rules and neither overrides the other. Use rules for file-type conventions, skills for procedures loaded on demand.

concepts.title: Project .claude/ vs ~/.claude/: which file goes where
concepts.titleEs: .claude/ del proyecto vs ~/.claude/: qué archivo va dónde
concepts.summary: Project .claude/ is committed and shared; ~/.claude/ is personal across projects (relocated by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). Both scopes: CLAUDE.md, rules/*.md, settings.json, skills/<name>/SKILL.md, commands/*.md, agents/*.md, output-styles/*.md, workflows/*.js, agent-memory/. Project only: settings.local.json (personal overrides, gitignored), .mcp.json at the repo root, .worktreeinclude. Global only: ~/.claude.json (app state, OAuth, personal MCP servers), projects/<project>/memory/, keybindings.json, themes/*.json.

concepts.title: Local session data, retention and purge
concepts.titleEs: Datos locales de sesión, retención y purga
concepts.summary: ~/.claude stores unencrypted data: transcripts at projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl, file-history/ checkpoint snapshots, plans/, debug/. The sweep deletes them after `cleanupPeriodDays` (default 30, minimum 1; 0 is a validation error) but never deletes auto memory or history.jsonl. `claude project purge <path>` (`--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--all`, `-i`) removes a project's transcripts, auto memory and history lines; `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` or `-p --no-session-persistence` avoids writing transcripts. Don't delete ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/plugins/.

concepts.title: How the prompt cache matches an exact prefix
concepts.titleEs: Cómo el caché de prompts coincide con un prefijo exacto
concepts.summary: Every turn re-sends the full context; the API reuses the longest exactly-matching prefix, so a change anywhere recomputes everything after it (no per-file caching). Requests are ordered system prompt (core instructions, tool definitions) → project context (CLAUDE.md, auto memory, unscoped rules) → conversation, so a new message leaves the first two cached while a system-prompt change invalidates everything. Each model has its own cache, and on most models each effort level too; the cache is effectively scoped to one machine and directory (worktrees don't share it).

concepts.title: Actions that break the cache vs actions that keep it
concepts.titleEs: Acciones que rompen el caché vs acciones que lo conservan
concepts.summary: Invalidate (one slow, costly turn): switching models (including `opusplan` plan-mode toggles and a skill whose frontmatter sets `model`), changing effort on most models, turning on fast mode, adding/removing MCP servers or denying a bare tool when tool search is off, toggling plugins, compaction, dropping accumulated images, upgrading Claude Code. Keep: editing repo files, editing CLAUDE.md (not applied until /clear, /compact or restart), permission mode changes, output style changes, invoking skills, /recap, /rewind (truncates to an already-cached prefix), spawning subagents. Pick model and effort at session start.

concepts.title: Cache lifetime: 5 minutes vs 1 hour
concepts.titleEs: Duración del caché: 5 minutos vs 1 hora
concepts.summary: The cache expires after inactivity; each hit resets the timer. Defaults: main conversation 1h on a Claude subscription within plan usage, 5m on usage credits, API key or cloud provider; subagents, workflows, compaction and other side requests 5m. Set `promptCacheTtl` (main) or `subagentPromptCacheTtl` to `5m` or `1h`. Precedence: FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 → the bucket's env var (CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL) → the bucket's setting → subagent `experimental.cacheTtl` → ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 → default.

concepts.title: claude --continue: reopen the most recent conversation here
concepts.titleEs: claude --continue: reabrir la conversación más reciente aquí
concepts.summary: `claude --continue` (`-c`) reopens the most recent conversation in the current directory, skipping `-p`/SDK sessions and sessions whose first prompt was /loop (`claude -p --continue` includes them) and refusing a background session that is still running. A resume restores history, model, agent, permission mode (from the terminal), active goal and unexpired scheduled tasks, but launch flags like `--mcp-config`, `--settings`, `--plugin-dir` and `--add-dir` must be passed again; settings files are re-read.

concepts.title: claude --resume and /resume: pick a specific session
concepts.titleEs: claude --resume y /resume: elegir una sesión concreta
concepts.summary: `claude --resume` (`-r`) opens the picker (Ctrl+A all projects, Ctrl+W all worktrees, Ctrl+B current branch, Ctrl+R rename, Space preview); `--resume <name|session-id|transcript.jsonl path>` resumes directly, and an ID works from any directory and is the only way back into a `-p` session. `--from-pr <number>` filters by pull request; `/resume` switches from inside a session. Name sessions with `claude -n <name>` or `/rename`. On Pro/Max, resuming a >100k-token session idle for over an hour offers Resume from summary vs Resume full session as-is.

concepts.title: /branch and --fork-session: try another direction safely
concepts.titleEs: /branch y --fork-session: probar otra dirección sin riesgo
concepts.summary: `/branch [name]` copies the conversation up to now into a new session ID and switches you into it; the original stays intact and reachable with `/resume`, and 'allow for this session' grants carry over because it's the same process. From the CLI, `claude --continue --fork-session` (or `--resume <id> --fork-session`) forks into a new process where you re-approve permissions. Resuming one session in two terminals without forking interleaves both into one transcript. Differs from /rewind (truncates in place) and /fork (runs a copy as a background session).

concepts.title: /usage: session cost, cache stats and plan breakdown
concepts.titleEs: /usage: costo de la sesión, estadísticas de caché y desglose del plan
concepts.summary: `/usage` (aliases `/cost`, `/stats`) shows the Session block (locally estimated cost for API users, token counts per model, reset by /clear), a `Prompt cache (main)` line with hit ratio, misses, likely cause and warm/cold state, and on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise a breakdown attributing usage to skills, subagents, plugins and MCP servers plus flags for behaviors over 10% (long context, cache misses). `/insights` instead writes an HTML report on how you work to ~/.claude/usage-data/report.html.

concepts.title: Reduce token usage: the highest-impact habits
concepts.titleEs: Reducir el uso de tokens: los hábitos de mayor impacto
concepts.summary: Usage climbs because every request resends the whole conversation, plus cache misses after breaks, scheduled tasks, subagents, teammates and compaction. Levers: /clear between tasks, Sonnet by default and Opus for hard reasoning (`model: haiku` for simple subagents), lower effort or `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` on fixed-budget models, disable unused MCP servers in /mcp and prefer CLIs like gh, move workflow instructions from CLAUDE.md into skills, delegate verbose work (tests, logs, research) to subagents, preprocess output with hooks, and write specific prompts.

concepts.title: Organization usage: OpenTelemetry and analytics dashboards
concepts.titleEs: Uso en la organización: OpenTelemetry y paneles de analytics
concepts.summary: Per-user tokens and cost across a team come from OpenTelemetry: set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`/`OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` (e.g. `otlp`) and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, usually in the managed settings `env` block (a repo's .claude/settings.json can't turn it on); prompt content stays redacted unless `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1`. Adoption and contribution dashboards live at claude.ai/analytics/claude-code (Team/Enterprise) and platform.claude.com/claude-code (Console API).

concepts.title: Where to launch and how to layer instructions in a monorepo
concepts.titleEs: Dónde lanzar y cómo escalonar instrucciones en un monorepo
concepts.summary: Launching from the repo root gives access to every file and loads the root CLAUDE.md (package files on demand); launching from a package limits access to that subtree and loads its CLAUDE.md plus every ancestor's. Use a per-directory CLAUDE.md when area owners maintain their own conventions, a path-scoped rule when conventions should live centrally in .claude/rules/. `claudeMdExcludes` (globs on absolute paths such as `**/packages/web/**`, arrays merge across scopes, usually in .claude/settings.local.json) skips other teams' CLAUDE.md and rules; managed CLAUDE.md can't be excluded. Project .claude/settings.json is not inherited from parent directories.

concepts.title: Cut what Claude reads: Read deny rules, code intelligence, sparse worktrees
concepts.titleEs: Reducir lo que Claude lee: reglas Read deny, code intelligence y worktrees dispersos
concepts.summary: Searches already respect .gitignore; for checked-in generated or vendored code add `permissions.deny` rules like `Read(./**/dist/**/*)` (the `/**/*` suffix still lets Claude ls/cd the directory). A code intelligence plugin (e.g. `/plugin install typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official`) replaces grep-and-read with go-to-definition. `worktree.sparsePaths` (directories relative to the repo root; include `.claude`) checks out only those paths plus root files in new worktrees, and `worktree.symlinkDirectories: ["node_modules"]` avoids duplicating it.

concepts.title: --add-dir vs additionalDirectories: reaching sibling packages
concepts.titleEs: --add-dir vs additionalDirectories: acceder a paquetes hermanos
concepts.summary: Both grant read/edit access outside the working directory. `permissions.additionalDirectories` in .claude/settings.json (paths relative to the launch dir, committed for the team) never loads the directory's CLAUDE.md, rules or skills. `claude --add-dir ../shared` or `/add-dir` loads its skills, and its CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/ and CLAUDE.local.md only when `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1` is set. `--add-dir` must be passed again when resuming.

concepts.title: The four settings files and who they reach
concepts.titleEs: Los cuatro archivos de settings y a quién alcanzan
concepts.summary: Pick the file by who the setting should affect: `~/.claude/settings.json` (user: you, every project), `.claude/settings.json` (shared project: commit it for the team), `.claude/settings.local.json` (project local: only you in this project; Claude Code saves 'Yes, and don't ask again' allow rules here and keeps it out of git) and managed settings (whole organization, nothing overrides them). `~/.claude.json` is a separate global-config file Claude Code writes itself (sign-in, MCP servers, trust decisions).

concepts.title: Settings precedence: which value wins
concepts.titleEs: Precedencia de settings: qué valor gana
concepts.summary: When the same key is set in several places the highest level wins, in this order: managed settings > command line (`--settings`, flags) > project local `.claude/settings.local.json` > shared project `.claude/settings.json` > user `~/.claude/settings.json`. List keys such as `permissions.allow` merge across files instead of overriding (except `fallbackModel`, `modelPicker` and a managed `availableModels`), and a few security keys honor a stricter lower-level value over managed, e.g. `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` from any scope.

concepts.title: Confirm what loaded and fix a broken settings file
concepts.titleEs: Confirmar qué cargó y arreglar un settings roto
concepts.summary: Run `/status` to read the `Setting sources` line (which files loaded, not which file supplied each key) and `claude doctor` to list rejected entries. Settings files are strict JSON: a `//` comment or trailing comma makes the whole file a Settings Error, while a single bad entry (malformed rule, unknown hook event) is a Settings Warning and is skipped. Most edits (permissions, hooks, env) reload live, but `model` and `effortLevel` are read at startup, so switch with `/model` or `/effort`; `/config` edits only a short list of personal options.

concepts.title: The env key: environment variables in settings
concepts.titleEs: La clave env: variables de entorno en settings
concepts.summary: The `env` key sets variables for every session and the subprocesses it starts; a value there overwrites the same variable exported in your shell, follows settings precedence between files, and `"VAR": ""` neutralizes a shell export you can't unset. Project and local files can't set variables like `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` or the OpenTelemetry exporter variables, and their `env` values apply only after you trust the workspace. For credentials use `apiKeyHelper` rather than plain-text `env`.

concepts.title: Override a setting for one session
concepts.titleEs: Sobrescribir un setting para una sola sesión
concepts.summary: Test a value without saving it via `claude --settings '<json or file>'` (above user/project/local, below managed; lasts one session), a key's own flag (`--model`, `--effort`) or its paired environment variable. Env vars aren't a precedence level: the winner is decided per pair, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` beats the `model` key from any file while `--model` beats both for the session. In-session commands usually save: `/model` writes your user default, but pressing `s` in the picker switches for this session only.

concepts.title: Why a committed setting doesn't apply
concepts.titleEs: Por qué un setting commiteado no se aplica
concepts.summary: A key in `.claude/settings.json` fails to reach teammates for two reasons: its Scope in the settings reference is `User or managed`, `User, local, or managed`, `Managed` or `Global config` (e.g. `permissions.defaultMode` values `auto`/`bypassPermissions`, the `autoMode` block), so a repo file is ignored; or it waits for workspace trust: `permissions.allow`, `permissions.additionalDirectories`, `extraKnownMarketplaces` and most `env` values apply only after each person trusts the folder, while `deny` and `ask` rules apply immediately. `claude -p` never shows the trust dialog.

concepts.title: Allow, ask and deny: evaluation order
concepts.titleEs: Allow, ask y deny: orden de evaluación
concepts.summary: Rules are evaluated deny first, then ask, then allow; the first match decides and specificity never changes the order, so `Bash(aws *)` in deny beats `Bash(aws s3 ls)` in allow, and a deny from any scope beats an allow from any other. A bare tool name in deny (`Bash`, `WebFetch`, `mcp__*`) removes the tool from Claude's context; a scoped rule (`Bash(rm *)`) only blocks matching calls. A PreToolUse hook returning `allow` can't bypass a deny or ask rule; view and edit rules with `/permissions`.

concepts.title: Writing Bash rules with wildcards
concepts.titleEs: Escribir reglas de Bash con comodines
concepts.summary: Write the command and replace the varying part with `*`, placed after the subcommand: `Bash(git log *)` allows only `git log`, `Bash(git *)` every git command; `Bash(ls *)` also matches bare `ls` but not `lsof`, and `Bash(ls:*)` is equivalent to `Bash(ls *)`. Compound commands (`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`) must match per subcommand and wrappers such as `timeout` or `nohup` are stripped, but rules match the text as written, so a `Bash(curl *)` deny doesn't stop `/usr/bin/curl` or `sh -c 'curl ...'`; use the sandbox or a PreToolUse hook when it must hold.

concepts.title: Path rules for Read, Edit and WebFetch
concepts.titleEs: Reglas de rutas para Read, Edit y WebFetch
concepts.summary: `Read(...)` and `Edit(...)` rules use gitignore patterns with four anchors: `//path` absolute from the filesystem root, `~/path` from home, `/path` relative to the settings source (project root for project/local files, `~/.claude` for user settings) and `path` or `./path` relative to the current directory. Write file rules as `Edit`, never `Write` (ignored with a warning); a `Read` deny such as `Read(./.env)` also blocks editing that path. `WebFetch(domain:example.com)` gates fetches by hostname. These rules cover Claude's tools and recognized commands like `cat`, not arbitrary scripts.

concepts.title: The permission modes and what each runs without asking
concepts.titleEs: Los modos de permisos y qué corre cada uno sin preguntar
concepts.summary: `default` (labeled Manual) runs only reads; `acceptEdits` adds file edits and filesystem commands (`mkdir`, `touch`, `mv`, `cp`, `rm`, `sed`) inside the working directory; `plan` reads and explores without editing source; `auto` runs everything behind a classifier; `dontAsk` runs only pre-approved tools and denies the rest; `bypassPermissions` runs everything. `Shift+Tab` cycles `default` → `acceptEdits` → `plan` (auto and bypass slot in when available; `dontAsk` only via `--permission-mode`). The starting mode comes from `--permission-mode`, then `permissions.defaultMode`, then the built-in default; deny rules block in every mode.

concepts.title: Plan mode: explore and propose before editing
concepts.titleEs: Plan mode: explorar y proponer antes de editar
concepts.summary: Plan mode has Claude read files, run exploratory commands and write a plan without editing your source. Enter it with `Shift+Tab`, by prefixing one prompt with `/plan`, with `claude --permission-mode plan`, or as a project default with `"permissions": {"defaultMode": "plan"}` in `.claude/settings.json`. When the plan is ready pick 'Yes, and use auto mode', 'Yes, manually approve edits' or 'No, keep planning'; `Ctrl+G` opens the plan in your editor to change it before approving.

concepts.title: dontAsk vs bypassPermissions for unattended runs
concepts.titleEs: dontAsk vs bypassPermissions para ejecuciones desatendidas
concepts.summary: `dontAsk` auto-denies anything not pre-approved, so it fits CI with an exact allowlist: `claude -p "..." --permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools "Bash(npm test)" "Read"`. `bypassPermissions` (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) skips prompts, including writes to protected paths like `.git`, `.claude` and `.mcp.json`; use it only in a container or VM, and Claude Code refuses it as root or under sudo. Explicit ask rules and `rm` of critical paths (`/`, `~`, the working directory) are never auto-approved in either; admins block bypass with `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"`.

concepts.title: How auto mode decides: rules, then the classifier
concepts.titleEs: Cómo decide auto mode: reglas y luego el clasificador
concepts.summary: In `auto` each action goes through a fixed order: your allow/ask/deny rules resolve first, read-only actions and working-directory edits are auto-approved, and everything else goes to a separate classifier model that blocks things like `curl | bash`, force pushes, production deploys or data leaving trusted infrastructure. Entering auto mode suspends broad allow rules (`Bash(*)`, `Bash(python*)`, `Agent`). After 3 consecutive or 20 total blocks it falls back to prompting, and blocked actions are listed in `/permissions` under Recently denied, where `r` retries one.

concepts.title: Tune the classifier with the autoMode block
concepts.titleEs: Ajustar el clasificador con el bloque autoMode
concepts.summary: Tell the classifier what you trust with prose entries in `autoMode.environment` (source control org, trusted buckets, internal domains, key services), set in `~/.claude/settings.json`, managed settings or `--settings`, never in `.claude/settings.json` or `.local.json`. Adjust rules with `autoMode.allow`, `soft_deny` and `hard_deny`: `hard_deny` blocks unconditionally, `soft_deny` blocks unless an `allow` exception or explicit user intent clears it. Include `"$defaults"` in each array or you replace the built-in list; inspect with `claude auto-mode defaults`, `config` and `critique`, or draft entries with `/auto-mode-setup`.

concepts.title: Human checkpoints in auto mode: ask, deny or say it
concepts.titleEs: Puntos de control en auto mode: ask, deny o decirlo
concepts.summary: Pick the boundary by how firm it must be: a content-scoped `permissions.ask` rule such as `Bash(git push *)` or `Bash(gh pr create *)` always forces a prompt even in auto mode; `permissions.deny` blocks before the classifier and nothing overrides it; a boundary said in conversation ('don't push until I review') is enforced by the classifier but can be lost to compaction. To approve a blocked action in conversation, name the action and its specifics (e.g. the branch of a force push); the approval covers that one action.

concepts.title: The sandboxed Bash tool and its two modes
concepts.titleEs: El Bash con sandbox y sus dos modos
concepts.summary: `/sandbox` turns on OS-level isolation (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2; no native Windows) for Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands and their child processes: by default they can write only to the working directory, added directories and a temp dir, can read almost everything, and a new network domain prompts. Auto-allow mode runs sandboxed commands without prompting (deny rules, content-scoped ask rules and critical-path `rm` still apply); regular-permissions mode keeps the prompts. Read/Edit tools, MCP servers and hooks are not sandboxed.

concepts.title: Sandbox settings keys and path conventions
concepts.titleEs: Claves de settings del sandbox y convenciones de rutas
concepts.summary: Configure the `sandbox` block: `enabled`, `filesystem.allowWrite` / `denyWrite` / `denyRead` / `allowRead`, `network.allowedDomains` / `deniedDomains`, `excludedCommands` (e.g. `docker *`), `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` to disable the `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` retry escape hatch, and `failIfUnavailable: true` to fail instead of running unsandboxed. Sandbox paths use normal conventions (`/tmp/build` is absolute; `./` is the project root in project settings but `~/.claude` in user settings), unlike permission rules where `//` means absolute; filesystem arrays merge across scopes.

concepts.title: Choosing an isolation boundary
concepts.titleEs: Elegir un límite de aislamiento
concepts.summary: Match isolation to the threat: the built-in Bash sandbox (shell commands only, everyday use), `npx @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime claude` (whole process incl. file tools, MCP servers and hooks, no Docker), a dev container (the Claude Code Dev Container Feature, non-root user, optional egress firewall), a custom container, a VM (strongest; untrusted repos) or a cloud session. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` should always run inside a container, VM or the sandbox runtime. In a dev container, persist login by mounting a volume at `~/.claude` and pointing `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at it.

concepts.title: How managed settings reach a machine
concepts.titleEs: Cómo llegan los settings administrados a una máquina
concepts.summary: Organizations deliver managed settings through server-managed settings in the claude.ai admin console (Teams/Enterprise; fetched at startup and polled hourly, the only source that reaches cloud sessions), MDM/OS policy (macOS `com.anthropic.claudecode` profile, Windows `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode`) or a `managed-settings.json` file (`/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`, `/etc/claude-code/`, `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`, plus `managed-settings.d/*.json`). By default the first source with a policy key wins, in the order remote > MDM > file > HKCU; `/status` names it, e.g. `Enterprise managed settings (file)`.

concepts.title: Managed-only locks an admin can set
concepts.titleEs: Bloqueos que solo puede fijar un admin
concepts.summary: Recognize the locks read only from managed settings: `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` (only managed permission rules count), `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly` and `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` (fail closed when the server fetch fails). `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` and `permissions.disableAutoMode` set to `"disable"` work from any file but are usually managed. Server-managed hooks, shell-command settings such as `apiKeyHelper` and some `env` variables need the user's approval in a security dialog.

concepts.title: Hard boundaries vs instructions: who enforces what
concepts.titleEs: Límites duros vs instrucciones: quién hace cumplir qué
concepts.summary: Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model: instructions in `CLAUDE.md` or a prompt shape what Claude tries but grant or revoke nothing, so hard boundaries need rules, a mode, a PreToolUse hook or the sandbox. Built-in prompt-injection defenses include trust verification for first-time folders and new MCP servers (skipped with `-p`), network commands like `curl` not auto-approved, WebFetch in a separate context window and a working-directory write boundary; with untrusted content, review commands and prefer a VM.

concepts.title: Training, retention and telemetry defaults
concepts.titleEs: Entrenamiento, retención y telemetría por defecto
concepts.summary: Commercial accounts (Team, Enterprise, API, cloud providers) aren't used for training and have 30-day retention; consumer accounts (Free, Pro, Max) train models only if the user allows it (then 5-year retention, otherwise 30 days). Claude Code keeps transcripts locally in plaintext under `~/.claude/projects/` for 30 days (`cleanupPeriodDays`), `/feedback` transcripts are kept 5 years, and `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING` or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` turn off optional traffic.

concepts.title: Zero Data Retention: scope and disabled features
concepts.titleEs: Zero Data Retention: alcance y funciones desactivadas
concepts.summary: Zero Data Retention is enabled per organization by Anthropic for qualified Claude for Enterprise accounts (not from admin settings): prompts and responses aren't stored after the response returns. It covers only sessions authenticated into that org (enforce with `forceLoginMethod` and `forceLoginOrgUUID`), not MCP servers or other third-party integrations, and it disables features that store data such as cloud sessions, Remote Control, artifacts and `/feedback`.

concepts.title: Skill vs CLAUDE.md vs .claude/rules: where instructions belong
concepts.titleEs: Skill vs CLAUDE.md vs .claude/rules: dónde van las instrucciones
concepts.summary: CLAUDE.md loads every session and holds 'always do X' facts (keep it under 200 lines); .claude/rules/ loads every session or only for matching paths; a skill loads on demand (description at start, body when invoked) and holds reference material or a workflow triggered with /<name>. Move a CLAUDE.md section into a skill when it has grown into a procedure, or when you paste the same playbook into chat repeatedly.

concepts.title: Skill vs hook vs subagent
concepts.titleEs: Skill vs hook vs subagente
concepts.summary: A hook always fires on a lifecycle event and is enforcement (a PreToolUse hook blocking .env edits), while a skill is instructions Claude interprets, so its outcome can vary. A subagent is an isolated worker with its own context window that returns only a summary; a skill adds to the main context. They combine: a subagent can preload skills via its skills field, and a skill can run isolated with context: fork.

concepts.title: Where skills load: enterprise, personal, project, nested, plugin, claude.ai
concepts.titleEs: Dónde se cargan las skills: enterprise, personal, proyecto, anidada, plugin, claude.ai
concepts.summary: ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md reaches all your projects on this machine (but not cloud sessions, Cowork or routines); .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is the project skill to commit, loaded from the start directory and every parent up to the repo root; <subdir>/.claude/skills/ loads only once Claude reads or edits files there (or after /add-dir); --add-dir loads the added directory's .claude/skills/ while permissions.additionalDirectories does not; plugin skills live in <plugin>/skills/. For routines, commit the skill to the repo or enable it on your claude.ai account.

concepts.title: Core frontmatter: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint
concepts.titleEs: Frontmatter básico: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint
concepts.summary: Frontmatter is read only when the opening --- is the file's first line; every field is optional, description is recommended (falls back to the first non-empty body line), and name defaults to the directory name. description + when_to_use are truncated at 1,536 characters in the listing, so put the key use case first; unknown fields are silently ignored, and malformed YAML loads the skill with no fields (/name works, auto-matching doesn't; find it with --debug or claude plugin validate). model and effort override the session only while the skill is active.

concepts.title: allowed-tools and disallowed-tools: per-turn tool grants
concepts.titleEs: allowed-tools y disallowed-tools: permisos por turno
concepts.summary: allowed-tools (e.g. `Bash(git add *) Bash(git commit *)`) lets Claude use the listed tools without prompting during the turn that invokes the skill; the grant clears when you send your next message, it restricts nothing, and deny/ask rules still override it. disallowed-tools removes tools from the pool while the skill is active. It is not gated by workspace trust, so review allowed-tools in repo skills; for session-wide approval use allow rules in settings instead.

concepts.title: context: fork and agent: run a skill in a subagent
concepts.titleEs: context: fork y agent: correr una skill en un subagente
concepts.summary: With context: fork, the SKILL.md content becomes the prompt of a new subagent of the type in agent (Explore, Plan, general-purpose by default, or a custom one from .claude/agents/); it does not see your conversation history, so it only makes sense for task skills, not pure guidelines. It runs in the background by default; set background: false to wait for the result in the invoking turn. It is the inverse of a subagent whose skills field preloads skills.

concepts.title: disable-model-invocation: true makes a skill user-only
concepts.titleEs: disable-model-invocation: true, solo tú la invocas
concepts.summary: Set disable-model-invocation: true for workflows with side effects or where you control timing (/deploy, /commit, /send-slack-message): only you can run it with /name, its description is removed from Claude's context (zero cost until invoked), it can't be preloaded into subagents, and a scheduled task won't run it. If Claude tries anyway, Claude Code blocks the call and Claude suggests you run it yourself.

concepts.title: user-invocable: false makes a skill Claude-only
concepts.titleEs: user-invocable: false, solo Claude la invoca
concepts.summary: user-invocable: false hides the skill from the / menu and typing /name doesn't run it, but its description stays in context and Claude can still invoke it; use it for background knowledge such as a legacy-system-context skill. It does not stop the Skill tool: to keep Claude from invoking a skill, use disable-model-invocation: true instead.

concepts.title: skillOverrides and Skill() permission rules
concepts.titleEs: skillOverrides y reglas de permiso Skill()
concepts.summary: skillOverrides in settings changes a skill's visibility without editing its SKILL.md: "on" (name + description, default when absent), "name-only", "user-invocable-only" (hidden from Claude, still in / menu) or "off" (hidden everywhere); the /skills menu cycles states with Space and saves to .claude/settings.local.json on Esc; plugin skills are not affected. Permission rules also gate the Skill tool: deny `Skill` disables all skills, `Skill(name)` matches exactly, `Skill(name *)` matches with any arguments.

concepts.title: $ARGUMENTS, $N and named arguments
concepts.titleEs: $ARGUMENTS, $N y argumentos con nombre
concepts.summary: $ARGUMENTS expands to the full string typed after /name; $ARGUMENTS[0] or $0 is the first argument (0-based, shell-style quoting so "hello world" is one); arguments: [issue, branch] in frontmatter makes $issue and $branch. If no placeholder receives the input, Claude Code appends ARGUMENTS: <value>; an unmatched $2 stays literal while an unmatched named argument becomes empty; escape a literal with \$1. Stacking /write-tests /fix-issue 123 loads up to six skills and passes 123 to each.

concepts.title: !`command` dynamic context injection
concepts.titleEs: Inyección de contexto dinámico con !`comando`
concepts.summary: A line like !`git diff HEAD` (the ! at line start or after whitespace) or a ```! fenced block runs before Claude sees the skill and is replaced by its output, run once and not re-scanned. Any non-zero exit (except exit 1 from search/compare commands) aborts the whole invocation, so append || true to checks; a deny rule, or outside auto mode any non-allow result, also aborts, so pre-approve the command in allowed-tools. disableSkillShellExecution: true replaces each command with a placeholder for user, project and plugin skills (not bundled or managed).

concepts.title: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} and other ${CLAUDE_*} substitutions
concepts.titleEs: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} y otras sustituciones ${CLAUDE_*}
concepts.summary: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is the directory holding SKILL.md, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} the project root, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} the session ID and ${CLAUDE_EFFORT} the current effort level; plugin skills also get ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}. Injected commands run in the session's current working directory, so reference bundled scripts with ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}; using the same variable in the body and in an allowed-tools Bash rule (Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/render.sh *)) lets the script run without a prompt.

concepts.title: Supporting files: keep SKILL.md lean
concepts.titleEs: Archivos de apoyo: un SKILL.md liviano
concepts.summary: A skill directory holds the required SKILL.md (overview and navigation) plus files such as reference.md and examples.md that Claude loads only when needed, and scripts/ that are executed, not loaded. Link each supporting file from SKILL.md saying what it contains and when to read it, and keep SKILL.md under 500 lines. Command files in .claude/commands/ can't have supporting files.

concepts.title: Skill content lifecycle and the skill listing budget
concepts.titleEs: Ciclo de vida del contenido y presupuesto del listado de skills
concepts.summary: Order: at session start only names and descriptions load (listing budget 1% of the context window, dropping descriptions of the least-invoked skills first) -> on invocation the rendered SKILL.md enters as one message and stays across turns without being re-read -> after auto-compaction the most recent invocation of each skill is re-attached, first 5,000 tokens each, 25,000 combined, newest first. Write standing instructions, not one-time steps; re-invoke after compaction if a skill fades. Use /skill-doctor to find costly unused skills, and skillListingBudgetFraction or "name-only" overrides when descriptions get cut.

concepts.title: paths: activate a skill only for matching files
concepts.titleEs: paths: activar una skill solo con ciertos archivos
concepts.summary: paths takes glob patterns (comma-separated string or YAML list) in the same format as path-specific rules in .claude/rules/; when set, Claude loads the skill automatically only while working with matching files. It limits automatic activation, not who may invoke it, and is not supported in .claude/commands/ files.

concepts.title: Custom commands are skills: .claude/commands/ vs .claude/skills/
concepts.titleEs: Los comandos personalizados son skills: .claude/commands/ vs .claude/skills/
concepts.summary: .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and behave the same; command files are the older format, accept the same frontmatter except name and paths, and have no supporting-file directory, so prefer a skill for new work. A file in a commands/ subdirectory is named with ':' (.claude/commands/frontend/component.md -> /frontend:component). Edits under skills directories are picked up live; run /reload-skills after creating a top-level skills directory mid-session.

concepts.title: Which skill runs when names collide
concepts.titleEs: Qué skill corre cuando los nombres chocan
concepts.summary: Precedence for the same name: enterprise > personal > project; a skill beats a .claude/commands/ file; your skill replaces a bundled command but not its aliases (a project code-review skill replaces /code-review, /review still runs the bundled one). Plugin skills always coexist as /plugin-name:skill-name, a nested skill stays reachable as /apps/web:deploy, and a claude.ai-synced skill loses its short name and runs as /anthropic-skills:<name>.

concepts.title: Bundled skills vs built-in commands
concepts.titleEs: Skills incluidas vs comandos integrados
concepts.summary: Bundled skills (marked Skill in the commands reference, e.g. /batch, /code-review, /debug, /loop, /doctor, /claude-api) are prompts that let Claude orchestrate with its tools, and Claude may invoke some on its own; built-in commands like /compact or /clear run fixed CLI logic and are not available through the Skill tool (except a few such as /init and /security-review). Turn bundled skills off with disableBundledSkills: true, or hide one with a skillOverrides entry set to "off".

concepts.title: /batch vs /simplify vs /code-review vs /debug vs /loop
concepts.titleEs: /batch vs /simplify vs /code-review vs /debug vs /loop
concepts.summary: /batch <instruction> researches a codebase-wide change, splits it into 5 to 30 units and, after you approve the plan, runs one background subagent per unit in its own worktree (needs a git repo or a WorktreeCreate hook). /simplify runs four parallel review agents for reuse, simplification, efficiency and abstraction cleanups (not bugs); /code-review looks for correctness bugs (--fix, --comment, ultra; alias /review); /debug turns on debug logging and reads the session log; /loop [interval] [prompt] repeats a prompt while the session is open.

concepts.title: /run, /verify and /run-skill-generator
concepts.titleEs: /run, /verify y /run-skill-generator
concepts.summary: /run launches and drives your app to see a change working; /verify builds and runs it to confirm a change without falling back to tests, and runs only when you invoke it. Both infer the launch from README, package.json or Makefile; when the project needs a database, env file or multi-step build, run /run-skill-generator once to record the recipe as a committed project skill at .claude/skills/run-<name>/. /verify can also record its own recipe at .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md, which then replaces the bundled /verify at the repo root.

concepts.title: Hooks guarantee behavior; CLAUDE.md only guides it
concepts.titleEs: Los hooks garantizan; CLAUDE.md solo orienta
concepts.summary: Hooks are handlers (shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tools, prompts or agents) that Claude Code runs automatically at lifecycle points, so an action always happens instead of depending on the model choosing it. Use CLAUDE.md for conventions ('we do it this way here') and hooks or permission rules for things that must always or never happen; use skills for extra instructions Claude invokes.

concepts.title: Common hook recipes: notify, format, protect, re-inject
concepts.titleEs: Recetas comunes: notificar, formatear, proteger, reinyectar
concepts.summary: Map a goal to event plus matcher: desktop alert when Claude waits -> Notification; run Prettier after edits -> PostToolUse with matcher "Edit|Write" piping jq -r '.tool_input.file_path'; block edits to .env or .git/ -> PreToolUse script that exits 2; restore key context after compaction -> SessionStart with matcher "compact" echoing text to stdout. A hook is added as a "hooks" block in a settings file such as ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json.

concepts.title: Event cadence and order in a session
concepts.titleEs: Cadencia y orden de los eventos en una sesión
concepts.summary: Order of a typical session: SessionStart -> UserPromptSubmit -> PreToolUse -> PermissionRequest -> PostToolUse (or PostToolUseFailure) -> PostToolBatch -> Stop (or StopFailure) -> SessionEnd, with PreCompact/PostCompact around compaction. SessionStart matchers are startup, resume, clear, compact and fork, and its plain-text stdout becomes context for Claude; UserPromptSubmit runs before Claude processes a prompt (default timeout 30 s) and can block it; SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5-second budget.

concepts.title: PreToolUse vs PostToolUse vs PostToolUseFailure
concepts.titleEs: PreToolUse vs PostToolUse vs PostToolUseFailure
concepts.summary: PreToolUse runs after Claude builds tool parameters and before the call executes, so it can block, ask or rewrite input; it does not fire for files added with @ in the prompt. PostToolUse runs only after a successful call and cannot undo it (updatedToolOutput only changes what Claude sees); failed calls fire PostToolUseFailure. To react to a file changing on disk whatever wrote it, use FileChanged, which runs after the change and cannot block.

concepts.title: Stop, SubagentStop and StopFailure: keep Claude working
concepts.titleEs: Stop, SubagentStop y StopFailure: que Claude siga trabajando
concepts.summary: Stop fires whenever the main agent finishes responding (not on user interrupt); a subagent finishing fires SubagentStop, and a turn ending on an API error fires StopFailure, whose output and exit code are ignored. Returning {"decision": "block", "reason": ...} or exiting 2 makes Claude continue with the reason; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext continues as non-error feedback. Check the stop_hook_active input field to exit early, since Claude Code overrides the block after 8 consecutive continuations (raise with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP).

concepts.title: Where a hook lives decides its scope
concepts.titleEs: Dónde vive un hook decide su alcance
concepts.summary: ~/.claude/settings.json covers all your projects; .claude/settings.json is committed and shared; .claude/settings.local.json is project-only and not shared; managed settings are org-wide; a plugin's hooks/hooks.json applies while it is enabled; skill frontmatter hooks register when the skill is invoked and last the rest of the session (once: true removes them after the first success); subagent frontmatter hooks run only while that subagent runs, with Stop converted to SubagentStop. Hook entries merge across levels, and there is no standalone hooks file for user or project config (not ~/.claude.json either).

concepts.title: Matcher groups: exact names, lists and regex
concepts.titleEs: Grupos de matcher: nombres exactos, listas y regex
concepts.summary: Config shape: "hooks": { "<Event>": [ { "matcher": "...", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "..." } ] } ] }. The matcher is a single string: "*", "" or omitted matches all; only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, , and | means an exact name or list ("Edit|Write"); any other character makes it an unanchored JavaScript regex ("Edit.*" also matches NotebookEdit, so anchor with ^$). Matching is case-sensitive, tool events match tool_name, MCP tools need "mcp__memory__.*", and some events (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, CwdChanged) ignore matchers.

concepts.title: The if field: filter by tool arguments
concepts.titleEs: El campo if: filtrar por argumentos de la herramienta
concepts.summary: The optional if field on a handler holds exactly one permission-rule pattern, such as "Bash(rm *)" or "Edit(*.ts)", checked after the matcher so the script only spawns when the tool arguments match; there is no && or list syntax, so use one handler per condition. It is evaluated only on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest and PermissionDenied (a hook with if on another event never runs), and it is best-effort, so use permission rules for a hard allow or deny.

concepts.title: What a hook receives on stdin
concepts.titleEs: Qué recibe un hook por stdin
concepts.summary: Command hooks get JSON on stdin (HTTP hooks as the POST body) with common fields session_id, transcript_path, cwd, permission_mode and hook_event_name, plus event fields such as tool_name, tool_input and tool_use_id; inside a subagent or with --agent they also get agent_id/agent_type. Reference scripts with ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} (fixed project root) and read cwd from the input when you need the directory Claude is currently in, for example inside a worktree.

concepts.title: Exit 0, exit 2 and every other exit code
concepts.titleEs: Exit 0, exit 2 y cualquier otro código
concepts.summary: Exit 0 is success: stdout goes to the debug log, except on UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart and PostModelSwitch where plain stdout becomes context for Claude. Exit 2 is a blocking error on events that can block (PreToolUse blocks the call, UserPromptSubmit erases the prompt, Stop keeps Claude working) and its stderr is the feedback; on PostToolUse it only shows stderr to Claude and on PermissionRequest it is ignored. Any other code, including 1, is a non-blocking error and the action proceeds, so policy hooks must use exit 2.

concepts.title: JSON output: universal fields, decision and hookSpecificOutput
concepts.titleEs: Salida JSON: campos universales, decision y hookSpecificOutput
concepts.summary: For structured control, exit 0 and print only a JSON object; stdout is parsed as JSON only if it starts with { and ends with }. Universal fields: continue (false stops Claude entirely and wins over decisions), stopReason, systemMessage (warning to the user); events like PostToolUse, Stop and UserPromptSubmit use top-level decision: "block" plus reason, while PreToolUse and PermissionRequest use hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName. Pick one approach per hook: exit 2 still blocks even if JSON says allow; string fields are capped at 10,000 characters.

concepts.title: PreToolUse permissionDecision: allow, deny, ask, defer
concepts.titleEs: permissionDecision en PreToolUse: allow, deny, ask, defer
concepts.summary: Return hookSpecificOutput { hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason, updatedInput, additionalContext }; the reason goes to Claude on deny and to the user on allow/ask. With several hooks the precedence is deny > defer > ask > allow, and updatedInput replaces the whole input object. PreToolUse fires before any permission-mode check, so deny blocks even in bypassPermissions, but allow never overrides deny or ask rules from settings; defer works only in -p mode for a single tool call.

concepts.title: PermissionRequest: answer the permission prompt for the user
concepts.titleEs: PermissionRequest: responder el diálogo de permisos por el usuario
concepts.summary: PermissionRequest fires only when Claude Code is about to show a permission prompt, and answers with hookSpecificOutput.decision: behavior "allow" (optionally updatedInput and updatedPermissions such as {type: "setMode", mode: "acceptEdits", destination: "session"}) or "deny" (message, interrupt). Exit 2 is not honored here, deny rules still win over allow, and in plain -p runs there is no prompt, so use PreToolUse there. Keep the matcher narrow (e.g. "ExitPlanMode"): an empty matcher auto-approves every prompt.

concepts.title: additionalContext: feed Claude dynamic facts
concepts.titleEs: additionalContext: darle a Claude datos dinámicos
concepts.summary: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is wrapped in a system reminder: at conversation start for SessionStart/SubagentStart, next to the prompt for UserPromptSubmit, next to the tool result for PreToolUse/PostToolUse, at turn end for Stop. Use it for changing state (branch, CI results, which test command applies) phrased as facts, and CLAUDE.md for static conventions; UserPromptSubmit cannot replace the prompt, only add context. On resume, mid-session context is replayed, not recomputed, while SessionStart reruns with source resume.

concepts.title: Command hooks: exec vs shell form, async
concepts.titleEs: Hooks de comando: forma exec vs shell, async
concepts.summary: A command handler has type "command", command, and optional args, shell ("bash" or "powershell"), async, asyncRewake, timeout (default 600 s) and statusMessage. With args it runs in exec form (no shell, each element one argument, best for ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} paths); without args it runs in shell form (sh -c, Git Bash on Windows) so pipes and && work. async: true runs it in the background: it cannot block, and its additionalContext/systemMessage arrive on the next turn; asyncRewake also wakes Claude on exit 2.

concepts.title: HTTP and MCP tool hooks
concepts.titleEs: Hooks HTTP y de herramienta MCP
concepts.summary: An http handler (url, headers, allowedEnvVars) POSTs the event JSON; only env vars listed in allowedEnvVars are interpolated into headers, and it cannot block through status codes: return 2xx with a JSON decision body instead (non-2xx and connection failures are non-blocking). An mcp_tool handler (server, tool, input with ${tool_input.file_path} substitution) calls a tool on a configured MCP server and reads its text like stdout; it is skipped on SessionStart at launch and on Setup because MCP servers are not ready yet.

concepts.title: Prompt and agent hooks: LLM judgment instead of a script
concepts.titleEs: Hooks prompt y agent: juicio de un LLM en vez de un script
concepts.summary: type "prompt" sends prompt (with $ARGUMENTS for the hook input) to a fast model, Haiku by default, for a single-turn check (default timeout 30 s); type "agent" spawns a subagent that can use Read, Grep and Glob for up to 50 turns (default 60 s, experimental). Both return {"ok": true} or {"ok": false, "reason": ...}; on Stop, ok false feeds the reason back so Claude keeps working. Use them for judgment calls, command hooks for deterministic rules; SessionStart supports neither, and PermissionRequest does not support agent.

concepts.title: Hooks run with your permissions: workspace trust and -p
concepts.titleEs: Los hooks corren con tus permisos: workspace trust y -p
concepts.summary: Command hooks execute with your full user permissions. In an interactive session Claude Code holds back hooks from every settings file until you accept the workspace trust dialog; in -p or SDK sessions the folder counts as trusted, so a repo's committed .claude/settings.json hooks run immediately. Before scripting claude -p over an unknown repo, review its .claude/ files, use --bare, or pass --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'; in scripts quote "$VAR", use absolute paths, and block .. path traversal.

concepts.title: disableAllHooks and managed hooks
concepts.titleEs: disableAllHooks y hooks administrados
concepts.summary: To remove a hook delete its entry; there is no per-hook disable. "disableAllHooks": true turns all hooks off and follows settings precedence, so a project's false overrides your user true, and --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' wins for one run. Managed hooks can only be disabled by disableAllHooks in managed settings, and allowManagedHooksOnly blocks user, project, local and plugin hooks (except plugins force-enabled by managed settings).

concepts.title: Diagnose a hook with /hooks and --debug
concepts.titleEs: Diagnosticar un hook con /hooks y --debug
concepts.summary: First run /hooks (read-only, shows event, matcher, type and source such as User/Project/Local Settings or Plugin Hooks): if the hook is missing, it is in the wrong file, a standalone file, or its file failed validation (e.g. a matcher array). If it shows but never fires, check a lowercase or misspelled matcher; then run claude --debug (log at ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt) or --debug-file <path>. If JSON has no effect, look for a shell-profile echo before the { or a field at the wrong level (debug log: 'Hook JSON output had unrecognized keys'); test scripts by piping sample JSON and checking echo $?.

concepts.title: Choose a parallel approach by who coordinates the work
concepts.titleEs: Elegir cómo paralelizar según quién coordina el trabajo
concepts.summary: Pick by coordinator: Claude delegates inside one conversation (subagents), you hand off and check back (agent view, `claude agents`), a lead supervises teammates (agent teams, experimental), or a script holds the plan (dynamic workflows). If tasks touch the same files, isolate them with worktrees; agent teams don't isolate teammates, so partition files instead.

concepts.title: Check on running work: /tasks, claude agents, /workflows
concepts.titleEs: Revisar trabajo en curso: /tasks, claude agents, /workflows
concepts.summary: `/tasks` lists everything running in the background of the current session (including subagents) and lets you attach or stop it; `claude agents` (from the shell) opens agent view for background sessions; `/workflows` shows workflow runs and phases. `/agents` is not the same as `claude agents`: it now only prints where subagent files live.

concepts.title: When a subagent beats the main conversation
concepts.titleEs: Cuándo un subagente es mejor que la conversación principal
concepts.summary: Use a subagent when a self-contained side task would flood your context with output you won't reuse (test runs, log digging, broad searches) or needs restricted tools: it works in its own context window and returns only a summary. Stay in the main conversation for iterative back-and-forth or shared multi-phase context; use a skill for reusable instructions that run in the main context, and `/btw` for a quick question about context you already have.

concepts.title: Built-in subagents: Explore, Plan, general-purpose
concepts.titleEs: Subagentes integrados: Explore, Plan, general-purpose
concepts.summary: Explore (read-only codebase search with quick/medium/very thorough levels) and Plan (research during plan mode) deny Write/Edit, skip CLAUDE.md and the git status snapshot, and are one-shot: they return no agent ID, so they can't be resumed. general-purpose has every subagent tool for explore-and-modify tasks; `claude` is the catch-all. Block one with a `permissions.deny` rule like `Agent(Explore)`, or remove Explore and Plan with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1`.

concepts.title: Invoke a subagent: natural language, @-mention, --agent
concepts.titleEs: Invocar un subagente: lenguaje natural, @-mención, --agent
concepts.summary: Naming a subagent in your prompt lets Claude decide; `@agent-<name>` (or picking it from the @ typeahead) guarantees it runs for one task; `claude --agent <name>` or `"agent": "<name>"` in `.claude/settings.json` makes the whole session use its system prompt, tools and model (the flag overrides the setting). Claude delegates automatically from the `description` field, and resumes a finished subagent with full history via `SendMessage` to its ID or name.

concepts.title: Where subagent files live and which one wins
concepts.titleEs: Dónde viven los subagentes y cuál gana
concepts.summary: When names collide, priority is: managed settings > `--agents` JSON flag (session only, not saved) > `.claude/agents/` (project, check into git; the one nearest the working directory wins) > `~/.claude/agents/` (all your projects) > a plugin's `agents/` directory. Identity comes only from the `name` frontmatter, not the filename or subfolder; plugin agents get a scoped name like `my-plugin:reviewer`.

concepts.title: Subagent frontmatter: tools, permissions, skills, memory, isolation
concepts.titleEs: Frontmatter del subagente: tools, permisos, skills, memoria, aislamiento
concepts.summary: Only `name` and `description` are required; the Markdown body is the system prompt. `tools` is an allowlist and `disallowedTools` a denylist applied first; `permissionMode`, `model`, `skills` (preloads full skill content), `mcpServers`, `hooks`, `memory` (user/project/local), `isolation: worktree`, `background`, `maxTurns` and `effort` tune the rest. Unknown or mis-cased keys are silently ignored, and plugin subagents ignore `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `permissionMode`.

concepts.title: How a subagent's model is resolved
concepts.titleEs: Cómo se resuelve el modelo de un subagente
concepts.summary: Order: the per-invocation `model` parameter > the definition's `model` frontmatter (`inherit` = main model) > `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` > the main conversation's model. To force one model onto every subagent, teammate and workflow agent, also set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1`; `/tasks` shows which model each subagent runs on.

concepts.title: Start an isolated session with --worktree
concepts.titleEs: Iniciar una sesión aislada con --worktree
concepts.summary: `claude --worktree <name>` (or `-w`) creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` on branch `worktree-<name>`, so parallel sessions never edit the same files; add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`.
