It branches from the remote default branch unless `worktree.baseRef` is `"head"`. On exit a clean worktree is removed automatically, one with changes prompts keep/remove, and `claude --worktree <name> --resume` returns to a kept one.

concepts.title: .worktreeinclude: copy gitignored files into worktrees
concepts.titleEs: .worktreeinclude: copiar archivos ignorados a los worktrees
concepts.summary: A worktree is a fresh checkout, so gitignored files like `.env` are missing. A `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root, in `.gitignore` syntax, copies files that match a pattern AND are gitignored into every worktree Claude creates with git (`--worktree`, subagent worktrees, desktop sessions); tracked files are never duplicated, and it isn't processed when a `WorktreeCreate` hook replaces git.

concepts.title: WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for non-git VCS
concepts.titleEs: Hooks WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove para VCS que no son git
concepts.summary: For SVN, Perforce, Mercurial or a custom location, a `WorktreeCreate` hook in `settings.json` replaces the git logic entirely: it reads the name from stdin JSON and prints the directory path to use; pair it with `WorktreeRemove` for cleanup. Copy local config files inside the hook, since `.worktreeinclude` is skipped.

concepts.title: Agent teams: a lead, teammates and a shared task list
concepts.titleEs: Agent teams: un lead, teammates y una lista de tareas compartida
concepts.summary: Enable with `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` (settings `env` or shell). The lead session spawns teammates, each a full Claude Code session that loads CLAUDE.md, MCP and skills but not the lead's history; they message each other directly and claim tasks from a shared list. Use teams when workers must discuss or challenge findings, subagents when only the result matters. Limits: one team per session, no nested teams, no worktree isolation (partition files), and a subagent Claude names launches as a teammate while teams are on.

concepts.title: Quality gates for teams: TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted
concepts.titleEs: Controles de calidad en equipos: TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted
concepts.summary: Hooks enforce team rules with exit code 2: `TeammateIdle` (a teammate is about to go idle: exit 2 sends feedback and keeps it working), `TaskCreated` (exit 2 blocks creation) and `TaskCompleted` (exit 2 blocks marking the task complete). Teammate permission prompts surface in the lead session, so pre-approve common operations before spawning.

concepts.title: Cross-session messaging between your own sessions
concepts.titleEs: Mensajes entre tus propias sesiones
concepts.summary: Claude finds your other sessions with `ListAgents` and sends plain-text findings with `SendMessage` (you can target one with `@<session-name>`); `/list-agents` shows who is reachable. A message never counts as your approval, can't change settings or CLAUDE.md, and slash commands in it don't run. Control inbound messages with `crossSessionInbound` (`accept`/`hold`/`refuse`), require approval before messages leave the machine with `isolatePeerMachines: true`, and block sending with deny rules on `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`.

concepts.title: Agent view: dispatch and supervise background sessions
concepts.titleEs: Agent view: lanzar y supervisar sesiones en segundo plano
concepts.summary: `claude agents` lists background sessions grouped by state (Needs input, Working, Completed, Failed, Stopped); type a prompt to dispatch a new one, `Space` to peek and reply, `Enter` to attach, `←` to detach. From the shell, `claude --bg "<prompt>"` (not with `-p`) starts one, and `claude attach/logs/stop/rm <id>` manage it. Each session moves into its own worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` before editing, unless `worktree.bgIsolation` is `"none"`.

concepts.title: Forked subagent: inherit the whole conversation
concepts.titleEs: Subagente fork: heredar toda la conversación
concepts.summary: A fork is a subagent that starts with the full conversation, same system prompt, tools and model, and shares the parent's prompt cache, so it's cheaper than a fresh subagent when the task needs lots of context; only its final result returns. Start one with `/subtask <task>`. Fork mode is on by default in interactive sessions (off with `-p`/SDK); `CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT` overrides it and an `Agent(fork)` deny rule stops Claude spawning forks.

concepts.title: /background vs /fork vs /subtask
concepts.titleEs: /background vs /fork vs /subtask
concepts.summary: `/background` (`/bg`, or `←` on an empty prompt) moves the current conversation into a background session and frees your terminal; `/fork` copies the conversation into a new, independent background session while you keep working; `/subtask` starts an in-session forked subagent whose result returns to your conversation. With agent view turned off, `/fork` starts the forked subagent and `/subtask` isn't available.

concepts.title: Dynamic workflows: when the script holds the plan
concepts.titleEs: Dynamic workflows: cuando el script tiene el plan
concepts.summary: A workflow is a JavaScript script (`agent()`, `pipeline()`, `parallel()`) that the runtime runs in the background, so intermediate results stay in script variables and Claude's context gets only the final answer; use it for codebase-wide audits, large migrations or cross-checked research (dozens to hundreds of agents). Trigger it with the `ultracode` keyword or by asking for a workflow, let Claude decide with `/effort ultracode`, or run `/deep-research`; watch, pause (`p`) or stop (`x`) runs in `/workflows`.

concepts.title: Save and rerun a workflow as a command
concepts.titleEs: Guardar y reutilizar un workflow como comando
concepts.summary: In `/workflows`, select a run and press `s` to save its script to `.claude/workflows/` (shared with the repo) or `~/.claude/workflows/` (personal); it then runs as `/<name>`, the project copy wins on a name clash, and input arrives in the `args` global. The file starts with `export const meta = { name, description }`. Turn workflows off with `disableWorkflows: true` or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1`.

concepts.title: /loop and session-scoped scheduled tasks
concepts.titleEs: /loop y tareas programadas de la sesión
concepts.summary: `/loop 5m <prompt>` runs on a fixed cron schedule, `/loop <prompt>` lets Claude pick each delay (1 min to 1 h), and a bare `/loop` runs the built-in maintenance prompt or your `loop.md` (`.claude/loop.md` beats `~/.claude/loop.md`). Tasks only fire while the session is open and idle, recurring ones expire after 7 days, and a new conversation clears them; for durable scheduling use Routines (cloud) or Desktop scheduled tasks.

concepts.title: /goal: keep working until a condition holds
concepts.titleEs: /goal: seguir trabajando hasta cumplir una condición
concepts.summary: `/goal <condition>` starts a turn immediately and, after each turn, a small fast model (Haiku by default) judges the condition not met (keep going), met or impossible (goal clears); `/goal` shows status and `/goal clear` removes it. It's a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook: the evaluator only reads the transcript, so write a condition Claude's output can prove (for example "`npm test` exits 0"). It doesn't change the permission mode; pair it with auto mode for unattended runs.

concepts.title: Channels: push external events into a running session
concepts.titleEs: Channels: empujar eventos externos a una sesión abierta
concepts.summary: A channel is a stdio MCP server declaring the `claude/channel` capability that emits `notifications/claude/channel` events (CI webhooks, Telegram/Discord/iMessage chats) into the open session; it can be two-way with a reply tool. Being in `.mcp.json` isn't enough: opt it in per session with `claude --channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace>`. Senders are gated by an allowlist, and Team/Enterprise admins must set `channelsEnabled: true` in managed settings. Research preview.

concepts.title: Add an MCP server and check that it connected
concepts.titleEs: Agregar un servidor MCP y comprobar que conectó
concepts.summary: Register a server with `claude mcp add` (defaults to local scope), then verify it with `claude mcp list` (statuses like `✔ Connected`, `! Needs authentication`, `✘ Failed to connect`, `⏸ Pending approval`), `claude mcp get <name>` or `/mcp` inside a session; remove it with `claude mcp remove <name>`. Its tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, the name used in permission rules and hook matchers, and every connected server costs context, so remove unused ones.

concepts.title: HTTP transport: the default for remote servers
concepts.titleEs: Transporte HTTP: el predeterminado para servidores remotos
concepts.summary: Use `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>` (optionally `--header "Authorization: Bearer ..."`) for hosted services; it is the recommended, most widely supported remote transport and supports OAuth. SSE (`--transport sse`) is deprecated, and WebSocket (`"type": "ws"`) can only be added via JSON (`claude mcp add-json`); in JSON an entry with `url` but no `type` is an error because a missing `type` means stdio.

concepts.title: stdio transport: a local process on your machine
concepts.titleEs: Transporte stdio: un proceso local en tu máquina
concepts.summary: Use `claude mcp add --transport stdio --env KEY=value <name> -- <command> [args]` for tools that need direct system access or custom scripts; everything after `--` goes to the server untouched, otherwise flags like `--port` are parsed as Claude's own. The spawned process receives `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (the project root) in its environment; in JSON the entry uses `command`, `args` and `env`.

concepts.title: Local scope: private to you, this project only (the default)
concepts.titleEs: Scope local: privado para ti y solo en este proyecto (el predeterminado)
concepts.summary: Local is the default scope: the server is stored in `~/.claude.json` under `projects.<project path>.mcpServers`, so it loads only in that project and only for you, which suits experiments and servers with credentials you won't commit. It is NOT `.claude/settings.local.json`; for the same server name, precedence is local > project > user > plugin > claude.ai connectors, and the winning entry is used whole (no field merging).

concepts.title: Project scope: a shared .mcp.json in the repo
concepts.titleEs: Scope de proyecto: un .mcp.json compartido en el repo
concepts.summary: `--scope project` writes `{"mcpServers": {"<name>": {"type": ..., "url"|"command", "args", "env", "headers"}}}` to `.mcp.json` at the project root, which you commit so teammates get it after approving a prompt (reset with `claude mcp reset-project-choices`; `claude -p` and SDK runs load it without asking, and `disabledMcpjsonServers` blocks it). Keep secrets out with `${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` expansion in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` and `headers`.

concepts.title: User scope: private to you, in every project
concepts.titleEs: Scope de usuario: privado para ti, en todos tus proyectos
concepts.summary: `--scope user` stores the server in the top-level `mcpServers` key of `~/.claude.json`, so it loads in all your projects but is never shared, which suits personal utilities. Scope is fixed at add time: to move a server, `claude mcp remove <name> --scope <old>` and re-add it; user scope loses to local and project definitions of the same name.

concepts.title: Authenticate remote servers: OAuth, headers or headersHelper
concepts.titleEs: Autenticar servidores remotos: OAuth, headers o headersHelper
concepts.summary: For OAuth servers, sign in from `/mcp` (or `claude mcp login <name>`, `--no-browser` over SSH); tokens refresh automatically and "Clear authentication" revokes them, and `--callback-port`/`--client-id` handle servers without dynamic client registration. For other schemes use static `headers` or a `headersHelper` command that prints a JSON object of headers within 10 seconds on every connect; a configured `Authorization` header disables the OAuth fallback, so a 401 shows as a failed connection.

concepts.title: MCP resources as @ mentions and prompts as slash commands
concepts.titleEs: Recursos MCP como menciones @ y prompts como comandos /
concepts.summary: Besides tools, a server can expose resources, which you attach by typing `@` and picking `@server:protocol://resource/path` (fetched as attachments), and prompts, which appear as `/servername:promptname (MCP)` and run as `/mcp__servername__promptname arg1 arg2` with whitespace-split arguments. Elicitation dialogs (form or URL mode) appear automatically when a server asks you for input mid-task.

concepts.title: Tool search and MCP output limits
concepts.titleEs: Tool search y límites de salida de MCP
concepts.summary: By default tool search defers MCP tool definitions (only names and server instructions load at start); `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` accepts `true`, `auto` (load upfront under 10% of context), `auto:N` or `false` (load everything upfront), and `"alwaysLoad": true` on a server entry exempts it. Outputs warn above 10,000 tokens and are capped at 25,000 by default (`MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` raises it); larger results are saved to a file Claude reads on demand.

concepts.title: managed-mcp.json vs managedMcpServers: fixed set or provided servers
concepts.titleEs: managed-mcp.json vs managedMcpServers: conjunto fijo o servidores provistos
concepts.summary: An admin-deployed `managed-mcp.json` (same format as `.mcp.json`, at `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`, `/etc/claude-code/` or `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`) takes exclusive control: users can't add servers and plugin and `--mcp-config` servers don't load; an empty `mcpServers` map disables MCP. `managedMcpServers` in managed settings instead provides https-only HTTP/SSE servers alongside users' own, and outranks every other scope.

concepts.title: allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers policy lists
concepts.titleEs: Las listas de política allowedMcpServers y deniedMcpServers
concepts.summary: The lists filter servers someone already added, matching entries of `serverUrl` (with `*` wildcards), `serverCommand` (exact command and args) or `serverName` (a label, not a security control). Evaluation order: merge lists from all scopes, then the denylist blocks (nothing overrides it), then the allowlist; an unset allowlist allows everything while `[]` allows none, and `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` ignores user/project allowlists.

concepts.title: What a plugin is and when to use one
concepts.titleEs: Qué es un plugin y cuándo conviene
concepts.summary: A plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers (and LSP servers) installed as one unit from a marketplace, e.g. `/plugin install commit-commands@claude-plugins-official`; keep standalone `.claude/` setups for one project or just you, and reach for a plugin to share, reuse across projects or version a setup. An enabled plugin is part of every session: its skill/agent names and descriptions cost context each turn, its MCP servers run and its hooks fire, so disable unused ones with `/plugin` or `claude plugin disable`.

concepts.title: Plugin install scopes and enabledPlugins
concepts.titleEs: Scopes de instalación de plugins y enabledPlugins
concepts.summary: Install scope decides where the `enabledPlugins` entry goes: user → `~/.claude/settings.json`, project → committed `.claude/settings.json` (each teammate still installs it once), local → `.claude/settings.local.json`; `claude plugin install` defaults to user. Precedence is local > project > user, and managed `enabledPlugins` (`true` forces, `false` blocks) beats all, so to opt out of a project-enabled plugin set it to `false` in `.claude/settings.local.json`; changes load on `/reload-plugins` or the next session.

concepts.title: Plugin trust: what it runs as you
concepts.titleEs: Confianza en plugins: lo que ejecuta con tus permisos
concepts.summary: A plugin's hooks and MCP/LSP server processes run with your user privileges outside the sandbox and permission rules; only Claude's tool calls (its MCP tools, Bash running plugin `bin/` executables) go through permissions. Before installing, read `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` and everything in `bin/`, and remember auto-update can change files later; only marketplaces sourced from `github.com/anthropics/` may use official or community names such as `claude-plugins-official`.

concepts.title: Plugin directory layout and namespacing
concepts.titleEs: La estructura de directorios de un plugin y su namespace
concepts.summary: Only `plugin.json` goes inside `.claude-plugin/`; at the plugin root go `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `agents/*.md`, `hooks/hooks.json` (top-level `"hooks"` key, same shape as settings), `.mcp.json`, `.lsp.json`, `bin/` (added to the Bash tool's PATH) and `settings.json` (only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` apply). Components saved inside `.claude-plugin/` don't load, and skills are namespaced by the plugin name, e.g. `/my-plugin:review`.

concepts.title: plugin.json: the plugin manifest
concepts.titleEs: plugin.json: el manifiesto del plugin
concepts.summary: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is optional, and `name` (kebab-case, namespaces every component) is its only required key; common keys are `version` (pins users until changed), `description`, `author`, `defaultEnabled`, `dependencies`, component path overrides (`skills`, `agents`, `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `lspServers`) and `userConfig` (each option needs `type`, `title`, `description`; `sensitive: true` stores it in secure storage). Unknown top-level keys are stripped with a validate warning, but unknown keys inside `userConfig` options fail the load.

concepts.title: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} vs ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} vs ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}
concepts.titleEs: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} vs ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} vs ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}
concepts.summary: Use `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for scripts and configs bundled with the plugin (it changes on every update, so never write state there), `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` (`~/.claude/plugins/data/<id>/`, kept across updates) for `node_modules`, caches and generated files, and `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` for project-local files. They resolve in hook `command`, MCP stdio `command`/`args`/`env`, remote `url`/`headers` and skill/agent bodies, but are not set in the Bash tool's environment.

concepts.title: marketplace.json: listing plugins in a marketplace
concepts.titleEs: marketplace.json: listar plugins en un marketplace
concepts.summary: A marketplace is a catalog at `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` requiring `name`, `owner` and `plugins`; each entry needs `name` (the install id before `@`, kept equal to the plugin.json name) and `source`: a relative path like `./plugins/foo` resolved from the marketplace root, or an object of type `github`, `url`, `git-subdir`, `npm`, `archive` or `command`. Users add it with `/plugin marketplace add owner/repo[#ref]`, a git URL, a `./` local path or a hosted JSON URL, then install `plugin@marketplace`.

concepts.title: Plugin versions and auto-update
concepts.titleEs: Versiones de plugins y actualización automática
concepts.summary: The computed version comes from, in order: `version` in plugin.json, then `version` in the marketplace entry, then the source (e.g. 12-char commit SHA); users get a new copy only when it changes, so either bump `version` every release or omit it in both places to track commits. Auto-update is on by default for Anthropic's official marketplaces and off for third-party ones (toggle in `/plugin` → Marketplaces or `autoUpdate` in `extraKnownMarketplaces`); updates apply on `/reload-plugins` or the next session.

concepts.title: Plugin dependencies and version constraints
concepts.titleEs: Dependencias entre plugins y restricciones de versión
concepts.summary: Declare `"dependencies": ["audit-logger", {"name": "secrets-vault", "version": "~2.1.0"}]` in plugin.json; bare names resolve in the same marketplace, `name@marketplace` in another (allowed via `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn`), and a semver range resolves to the highest `<name>--v<version>` git tag. Installing a plugin also installs its dependencies at the same scope; non-overlapping ranges fail with `has conflicting version requirements`, and auto-installed dependencies stay after uninstall until `claude plugin prune`.

concepts.title: Develop and debug a plugin: --plugin-dir, validate, reload
concepts.titleEs: Desarrollar y depurar un plugin: --plugin-dir, validate y reload
concepts.summary: Load a work-in-progress plugin for one session with `claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin` (no marketplace, nothing written to settings; it overrides a same-named installed plugin), and after edits run `/reload-plugins`. When something doesn't show up, check in order: `claude plugin validate <path>` (manifest and frontmatter, `--strict` for CI), `/reload-plugins`, the `/plugin` Installed and Errors tabs, then `claude plugin list`; a plugin must be declared in settings, fetched to `~/.claude/plugins/`, and loaded in the session.

concepts.title: claude plugin eval: test behavior against a no-plugin baseline
concepts.titleEs: claude plugin eval: probar el comportamiento contra una línea base sin plugin
concepts.summary: `claude plugin eval` runs cases from the plugin's `evals/` directory (each a prompt plus graders such as regex, tool-called or model-judged rubric) in isolated non-interactive sessions, 3 runs per case by default, and compares WITH vs W/OUT the plugin so Δ shows what the plugin contributed; `claude plugin eval init` drafts the suite. Unlike `validate`, it tests behavior, costs real model calls on your account, and can gate CI via `--threshold` (default 1.0).

concepts.title: claude plugin details: measure a plugin's always-on cost
concepts.titleEs: claude plugin details: medir el costo permanente de un plugin
concepts.summary: Run `claude plugin details <name>` in your shell (not in a session) to print the Component inventory and the Always-on token figure: the names and descriptions of skills, agents and commands added to every session, plus per-component always-on vs on-invoke costs. Hooks and MCP servers aren't estimated there (use `/context` for MCP tools), and the `/plugin` Installed tab's "Not used recently" group points at plugins worth disabling.

concepts.title: claude -p: one-shot non-interactive runs
concepts.titleEs: claude -p: ejecuciones no interactivas de una sola vez
concepts.summary: `claude -p "..."` (or `--print`) runs a task non-interactively, reads piped stdin (capped at 10MB) and exits 0 on success or non-zero on failure; SIGTERM exits 143 without finishing the turn. User-invoked skills work by putting `/skill-name` in the prompt, terminal-only commands like `/login` don't; chain runs with `--continue` (most recent conversation) or `--resume <session_id>` captured via `--output-format json | jq -r '.session_id'`.

concepts.title: --bare: skip auto-discovery for reproducible scripts
concepts.titleEs: --bare: saltar el autodescubrimiento para scripts reproducibles
concepts.summary: `--bare` skips hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md, never reads OAuth or the keychain (so set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` in `--settings`), and leaves only Bash, file read and file edit tools. Pass context back explicitly with `--append-system-prompt[-file]`, `--settings`, `--mcp-config`, `--agents` and `--plugin-dir`; without `--bare`, `-p` runs a project's `.claude/settings.json` hooks and `.mcp.json` servers with no trust dialog.

concepts.title: Pre-approving tools for unattended -p runs
concepts.titleEs: Preaprobar herramientas en ejecuciones -p desatendidas
concepts.summary: In `-p` the starting mode is Manual, so pre-approve with `--allowedTools` using permission rule syntax (`Bash(git diff *)`: the space before `*` matters) or set a baseline with `--permission-mode` (`dontAsk` denies anything that would prompt, `acceptEdits` auto-writes files, `auto` uses the classifier). `--permission-prompts none` stops waiting on a permission host (a `canUseTool` callback or `--permission-prompt-tool` MCP tool) and denies what would prompt unless a `PermissionRequest` hook allows it.

concepts.title: text vs json vs stream-json output
concepts.titleEs: Salida text vs json vs stream-json
concepts.summary: `--output-format text` (default) prints plain text; `json` returns one object with `result`, `session_id`, `total_cost_usd` and usage; `stream-json` emits newline-delimited events (use `--verbose`, plus `--include-partial-messages` for token deltas) that start with `system/init` and end with a `result` message. Subagent messages carry a non-null `parent_tool_use_id`, and a CI gate can fail when `system/init` lists `plugin_errors` or `mcp_server_errors`.

concepts.title: Structured output with --json-schema / outputFormat
concepts.titleEs: Salida estructurada con --json-schema / outputFormat
concepts.summary: CLI: `--output-format json --json-schema '<schema>'` puts validated data in `structured_output`; SDK: `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema", schema }` (Python `output_format`), with Zod converted using `target: "draft-7"` because the SDK validates draft-07. An invalid schema fails at startup, `format` is an unenforced annotation, and a run that can't satisfy the schema ends with subtype `error_max_structured_output_retries`; treat `success` without `structured_output` as a failure too.

concepts.title: Agent SDK vs CLI vs Client SDK vs Managed Agents
concepts.titleEs: Agent SDK vs CLI vs Client SDK vs Managed Agents
concepts.summary: Use the Agent SDK (Python/TypeScript) to embed Claude Code's loop, built-in tools, permissions, sessions and hooks in a process you operate; it bundles a native `claude` binary. Use the CLI for interactive work or `claude -p --output-format json` from other languages, the Client SDK to call the Claude API and write the tool loop yourself, and Managed Agents to have Anthropic host the loop; SDK products must authenticate with an API key (or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry), not claude.ai login.

concepts.title: The agent loop, message types and ResultMessage subtypes
concepts.titleEs: El loop, los tipos de mensaje y los subtypes de ResultMessage
concepts.summary: `query()` yields messages in order: SystemMessage `init`, AssistantMessage/UserMessage per turn (optional StreamEvent), then a ResultMessage whose `subtype` is `success`, `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`, `error_during_execution` or `error_max_structured_output_retries`; `result` exists only on `success`, while `total_cost_usd`, `usage`, `num_turns` and `session_id` are always present. `maxTurns` counts tool-use turns and `maxBudgetUsd` includes subagent spend (no limit by default); a single-shot `query()` raises after yielding an error result, so wrap it in try.

concepts.title: settingSources: which filesystem config the SDK loads
concepts.titleEs: settingSources: qué configuración del disco carga el SDK
concepts.summary: Omitting `settingSources` equals `["user", "project", "local"]`: `user` loads `~/.claude/` settings, CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, commands and agents; `project` loads `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` and hooks, CLAUDE.md and rules up the tree, and project skills/agents; `local` loads `CLAUDE.local.md` and `settings.local.json`. `settingSources: []` limits the agent to programmatic options, but managed policy settings, `~/.claude.json` and auto memory still load regardless.

concepts.title: Custom tools on an in-process SDK MCP server
concepts.titleEs: Herramientas propias en un servidor MCP del SDK en proceso
concepts.summary: Define a tool with name, description, input schema (Zod in TypeScript, a type dict or JSON Schema in Python) and an async handler returning `content` (plus optional `structuredContent` and `isError: true` for failures), wrap it with `createSdkMcpServer` / `create_sdk_mcp_server`, and pass it in `mcpServers`. The key becomes the server segment of `mcp__{server}__{tool}`, which you list (or wildcard `mcp__weather__*`) in `allowedTools`; set `readOnlyHint` so the tool can run in parallel.

concepts.title: External MCP servers and tool search in the SDK
concepts.titleEs: Servidores MCP externos y tool search en el SDK
concepts.summary: Pass servers in `mcpServers` (or `.mcp.json` via the `project` source): a command means stdio, a URL means `type: "http"` or `"sse"`; credentials go in `env` or `headers` since the SDK runs no interactive OAuth. MCP tools need `allowedTools` (`acceptEdits` doesn't approve them), and the init message reports each server as `pending`, `connected`, `failed`, `needs-auth` or `disabled`. Tool search is on by default and defers schemas; tune it with `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` (`true`, `auto`, `auto:N`, `false`).

concepts.title: Programmatic subagents with AgentDefinition
concepts.titleEs: Subagentes programáticos con AgentDefinition
concepts.summary: Pass `agents: { name: AgentDefinition }` with required `description` and `prompt` and optional `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `skills`, `mcpServers`, `maxTurns`, `background`, `effort` and `permissionMode`; Claude calls them through the `Agent` tool, and programmatic definitions override `.claude/agents/` files with the same name. A subagent starts fresh and only gets the Agent tool's prompt string; cap growth with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (default 3), `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` (default 20) and `maxBudgetUsd`.

concepts.title: SDK permission order and the canUseTool callback
concepts.titleEs: El orden de permisos del SDK y el callback canUseTool
concepts.summary: A tool call is checked in order: hooks, deny rules, ask rules, permission mode, allow rules, then the `canUseTool` callback (skipped and denied in `dontAsk`). Anything approved earlier never reaches `canUseTool`, and `allowedTools` doesn't restrict `bypassPermissions`; a bare `disallowedTools` name removes the tool from context. The callback also receives `AskUserQuestion` and returns `{ behavior: "allow", updatedInput }` or `{ behavior: "deny", message }`.

concepts.title: Hook callbacks passed to query()
concepts.titleEs: Hooks como callbacks pasados a query()
concepts.summary: `hooks: { PreToolUse: [{ matcher: "Write|Edit", hooks: [callback] }] }` runs in your process alongside filesystem hooks loaded via `settingSources`; a callback returns `{}` to allow, or `hookSpecificOutput` with `permissionDecision` (`allow`/`deny`/`ask`/`defer`), `permissionDecisionReason`, `updatedInput`, or `additionalContext` on PostToolUse. Matching hooks run in parallel and precedence is deny > defer > ask > allow; an async output only suits side effects like logging.

concepts.title: System prompt: minimal default, claude_code preset, append or custom
concepts.titleEs: System prompt: mínimo, preset claude_code, append o personalizado
concepts.summary: Without `systemPrompt` the SDK uses a minimal tool-calling prompt (unlike `claude -p`, which uses Claude Code's); `{ type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append: "..." }` keeps tool guidance and safety rules and adds yours, and a custom string replaces everything. CLI equivalents: `--append-system-prompt[-file]` adds, `--system-prompt[-file]` replaces (mutually exclusive). CLAUDE.md is injected separately via `settingSources`, and a changed prompt on a resumed session applies only after compaction.

concepts.title: SDK sessions: continue vs resume vs fork
concepts.titleEs: Sesiones del SDK: continue vs resume vs fork
concepts.summary: `continue: true` (Python `continue_conversation=True`) resumes the most recent session in the directory; `resume: sessionId` returns to a specific one, with the ID read from the ResultMessage `session_id`; forking creates a new session ID from a copy of the history and leaves the original unchanged. Transcripts live in `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` and persist the conversation, not files; `persistSession: false` (TypeScript) keeps nothing on disk, and a `SessionStore` enables cross-host resume.

concepts.title: File checkpointing and rewindFiles
concepts.titleEs: File checkpointing y rewindFiles
concepts.summary: Set `enableFileCheckpointing: true` plus `extraArgs: { 'replay-user-messages': null }` so each user message carries a UUID checkpoint, then call `rewindFiles(uuid)` (`rewind_files` in Python) to delete created files and restore modified ones. Only Write, Edit and NotebookEdit changes are tracked (not Bash, not subagent edits), and the conversation isn't rewound; from the CLI: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING=true claude -p --resume <id> --rewind-files <uuid>`.

concepts.title: Reading cost and usage from SDK results
concepts.titleEs: Leer costo y uso en los resultados del SDK
concepts.summary: `total_cost_usd` on the result is a client-side estimate for development and budgeting, not billing (use the Usage and Cost API for that); it includes subagents, `usage` counts only the top-level loop, and `modelUsage` (`model_usage` in Python) gives whole-tree per-model accounting. A resumed call reports the session's whole spend, but `maxBudgetUsd` counts only that call's own spend; in streaming input mode read the latest result rather than summing.

concepts.title: Hosting patterns: ephemeral, long-running, hybrid, multi-agent
concepts.titleEs: Patrones de hosting: efímero, persistente, híbrido, multiagente
concepts.summary: Each `query()` spawns a `claude` subprocess that owns a shell, cwd and local JSONL transcripts, so N sessions means N subprocesses and local state dies with the container. Pick ephemeral (container per task), long-running (persistent containers holding sessions via `streamInput()` or `ClaudeSDKClient`), hybrid (containers spin down and rehydrate, requiring a `SessionStore` with `append` and `load`) or multi-agent (one container, a separate `cwd` per agent).

concepts.title: Multi-tenant isolation and the credential proxy pattern
concepts.titleEs: Aislamiento multi-tenant y el patrón de proxy de credenciales
concepts.summary: To isolate tenants in a shared container, combine `settingSources: []`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` in `env`, a per-tenant `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and an explicit per-tenant `cwd`. Keep credentials outside the agent's boundary with a proxy that injects them: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` routes only sampling requests to it, while `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` route all traffic; isolation options range from sandbox-runtime and Docker (`--network none`) to gVisor and VMs.

concepts.title: OpenTelemetry export from the SDK
concepts.titleEs: Exportar OpenTelemetry desde el SDK
concepts.summary: Telemetry is off until `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and at least one exporter is set: `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` (tokens, cost), `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` (events) and `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` plus `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1` (spans `claude_code.interaction`, `llm_request`, `tool`). Set them in the process environment or the `env` option, never use the `console` exporter (stdout is the SDK's message channel), and shorten export intervals for short-lived runs.

concepts.title: Setting up claude-code-action: app, secrets and auth
concepts.titleEs: Configurar claude-code-action: app, secrets y autenticación
concepts.summary: `/install-github-app` (github.com only, needs `gh` and repo admin) installs the Claude GitHub App, saves a secret and opens a workflow PR; manually, install the app, add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (passed as `anthropic_api_key`) or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` (passed as `claude_code_oauth_token`), and copy `claude.yml` to `.github/workflows/`. Shared org secrets should be API keys, not personal OAuth tokens; `use_bedrock`, `use_vertex` or `use_foundry` route inference through a cloud via OIDC.

concepts.title: Interactive vs automation mode and claude_args
concepts.titleEs: Modo interactivo vs automatización y claude_args
concepts.summary: With no `prompt` input the action runs in interactive mode and answers the `trigger_phrase` (default `@claude`) in comments; with a `prompt` (plain text, `/skill-name` after `actions/checkout`, or `/plugin:skill` with `plugins`) it runs in automation mode on any event, including cron. `claude_args` passes CLI flags such as `--max-turns`, `--model`, `--allowedTools` and `--mcp-config`; triggering users need write access and bots are rejected unless listed in `allowed_bots`.

concepts.title: Claude Code in GitLab CI/CD
concepts.titleEs: Claude Code en GitLab CI/CD
concepts.summary: The GitLab integration is in beta and maintained by GitLab: add a Claude job to `.gitlab-ci.yml` and a masked `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` CI/CD variable (or AWS OIDC / GCP Workload Identity Federation for Bedrock or Agent Platform), use `CI_JOB_TOKEN` or a `GITLAB_ACCESS_TOKEN` project token for GitLab API calls, and wire `@claude` mentions through a webhook listener that triggers the pipeline. Changes arrive as MRs; `/install-github-app` does not work for GitLab remotes.

concepts.title: claude-cli:// deep links
concepts.titleEs: Deep links claude-cli://
concepts.summary: `claude-cli://open?q=<url-encoded prompt>&repo=owner/name` (or `cwd=<absolute path>`, which wins over `repo`) opens a local terminal session with the prompt pre-filled but never sent, showing a `Prompt from an external link` warning. The handler registers on the first prompt of an interactive session, GitHub-rendered Markdown won't make the link clickable, and `disableDeepLinkRegistration: "disable"` in settings prevents registration.

concepts.title: Cloud sessions: what runs where and what config carries over
concepts.titleEs: Sesiones en la nube: dónde corren y qué configuración llega
concepts.summary: A cloud session runs on an Anthropic-managed Ubuntu 24.04 VM from a fresh GitHub clone, keeps running after you disconnect, and is started from claude.ai/code, the mobile Code tab, Desktop with Cloud selected, or claude --cloud; GitHub access comes from the Claude GitHub App or /web-setup (your gh token). Only what is committed carries over (CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json hooks and permission rules, .mcp.json, .claude/rules, skills, agents, commands) while ~/.claude files, local/user-scope MCP servers and plugins in enabledPlugins do not, and cloud permission modes are Accept edits, Plan and Auto (no Bypass).

concepts.title: --cloud vs --teleport vs --resume: moving work between terminal and cloud
concepts.titleEs: --cloud vs --teleport vs --resume: mover trabajo entre terminal y nube
concepts.summary: claude --cloud "task" creates a new cloud session that clones your current branch from the GitHub remote (push first; with no remote or no GitHub App it uploads a bundle, forced with CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1), and claude -p "msg" --cloud <session-id> queues a follow-up into an existing one. claude --teleport (or /teleport, /tp) pulls a cloud session and its branch into your terminal and requires a clean working tree, the same repo (not a fork), the branch pushed and the same claude.ai account, whereas --resume only lists this machine's local history; the CLI cannot push an existing terminal session to the cloud.

concepts.title: Cloud environments: network levels, setup scripts and SessionStart hooks
concepts.titleEs: Entornos cloud: niveles de red, setup scripts y hooks SessionStart
concepts.summary: Each environment sets one network level (None, Trusted = default allowlist of registries and GitHub, Full, or Custom with your own Allowed domains), .env-format variables that everyone using it can read (no secrets), and a setup script that runs as root before Claude Code launches, must exit 0, and is cached as a filesystem snapshot only if it finishes in about five minutes. Order at session start: setup script (skipped when cached, cloud only) then SessionStart hooks from the repo's .claude/settings.json (every start and resume, local and cloud; gate with CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true); /remote-env picks the default environment for claude --cloud.

concepts.title: Routines and their triggers: schedule, API and GitHub
concepts.titleEs: Routines y sus triggers: schedule, API y GitHub
concepts.summary: A routine is a saved prompt, repositories, environment and connectors that runs autonomously as a cloud session (no permission-mode picker, pushes to claude/ branches, acts as your GitHub identity) and is created at claude.ai/code/routines or with /schedule. Triggers combine freely: schedule (hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly or one-off; minimum interval one hour; custom cron via /schedule update), API (POST to the routine's /fire endpoint with its bearer token; the optional text field arrives in an untrusted <routine-fire-payload> block the prompt must explicitly reference), and GitHub pull_request or release events with filters, which need the Claude GitHub App installed (/web-setup is not enough).

concepts.title: Cloud routine vs Desktop scheduled task vs /loop
concepts.titleEs: Routine en la nube vs tarea programada de Desktop vs /loop
concepts.summary: Cloud routines run without your machine (fresh clone, connectors, minimum 1 hour); Desktop scheduled tasks run on your machine with local files, only while the app is open and the computer awake (minimum 1 minute, per-task permission mode, prompt stored in ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/<name>/SKILL.md, and after sleep only one catch-up run for the most recent miss in the last seven days); /loop polls only inside an open session. In Desktop, Routines > New routine > Cloud makes a routine and > Local makes a scheduled task.

concepts.title: Auto-fix: let Claude watch a PR for CI failures and review comments
concepts.titleEs: Auto-fix: que Claude vigile un PR por fallos de CI y comentarios
concepts.summary: Auto-fix is a per-PR toggle (from the cloud session's CI status bar, /autofix-pr on the PR's branch, or by asking Claude) that needs the Claude GitHub App and subscribes a cloud session to that PR's CI failures and review comments, pushing clear fixes and asking about ambiguous ones. It cannot react to merge conflicts, and its replies post under your GitHub user, so they can trigger issue_comment automation such as Atlantis.

concepts.title: Managed Code Review: triggers, severities and REVIEW.md
concepts.titleEs: Code Review administrado: disparadores, severidades y REVIEW.md
concepts.summary: Code Review (Team and Enterprise) is enabled by an Owner in admin settings with the Claude GitHub App; each repo's Review Behavior is Once after PR creation, After every push, or Manual, and a top-level @claude review comment starts a one-off review while @claude review always also subscribes the PR to push-triggered reviews (fork PRs only review on a comment). Findings are Important, Nit or Pre-existing and never approve or block; tune them with a root REVIEW.md (severity, nit cap, skip rules, always-check rules) while CLAUDE.md violations are flagged as nits.

concepts.title: /code-review vs /code-review ultra vs claude ultrareview
concepts.titleEs: /code-review vs /code-review ultra vs claude ultrareview
concepts.summary: /code-review reviews your branch plus uncommitted changes (or a path, PR number, branch or range) locally as a background subagent, with low/medium effort for fewer high-confidence findings and high/max for broader coverage, --fix to apply findings and --comment to post them; it follows CLAUDE.md but not REVIEW.md. /code-review ultra launches a verified multi-agent fleet in a cloud sandbox (about 5-10 minutes, free runs then usage credits, claude.ai auth only, never started by Claude on its own), and claude ultrareview is the blocking CI form with --json, --timeout (default 45) and exit codes 0, 1 and 130.

concepts.title: security-guidance vs Claude Security plugin vs /security-review
concepts.titleEs: security-guidance vs plugin Claude Security vs /security-review
concepts.summary: The security-guidance plugin runs automatically while Claude writes code at three depths: a per-edit pattern match (no model call), an end-of-turn background review of the git diff, and an agentic review on commits or pushes Claude makes, never blocking writes; extend it with claude-security-guidance.md and security-patterns.yaml. The Claude Security plugin is on-demand: /claude-security scans the repo or a diff with verified agents, writes a CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/ report and patches/F<n>.patch files that are never applied automatically, while /security-review is a single pass over the current branch and Code Review covers the PR.

concepts.title: Remote Control: drive a local session from phone or browser
concepts.titleEs: Remote Control: manejar una sesión local desde el móvil o el navegador
concepts.summary: Remote Control connects claude.ai/code or the Claude app to a session that keeps running on your machine, so local files, MCP servers and config stay available but the computer must stay on. Start it as server mode with claude remote-control (--spawn same-dir|worktree|session, --capacity default 32), as an interactive session with claude --remote-control (--rc), or mid-session with /remote-control (/rc) which carries the history; it needs a claude.ai subscription (no API key, Bedrock or custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL), uses outbound HTTPS only, auto-connects with remoteControlAtStartup: true in user or managed settings, and is unrelated to --cloud.

concepts.title: The Claude app's Code tab: which remote surface to use
concepts.titleEs: La pestaña Code de la app Claude: qué superficie remota usar
concepts.summary: The Claude app runs no code: from its Code tab you reach cloud sessions and Projects (keep going with the laptop closed), Remote Control sessions (need your machine on, local tools) or Dispatch (a Pro/Max task sent to the Desktop app). Cloud sessions offer Accept edits, Plan and Auto; Remote Control offers Manual, Accept edits and Plan; Bypass is never selectable from the app, and terminal-only commands like /plugin and /resume don't work remotely while /compact, /clear, /context and /model <name> do.

concepts.title: Projects: one conversation that coordinates parallel cloud threads
concepts.titleEs: Projects: una conversación que coordina hilos en la nube en paralelo
concepts.summary: A Project (Pro/Max beta, at claude.ai/code, Desktop and mobile, not the CLI) is a coordinating conversation where Claude starts a thread per task, usually a cloud session on its own branch, and the Overview pane shows what is ready or waiting on you. Every thread starts with the project instructions (up to 16,000 characters), project memory indexed by MEMORY.md and each repo's CLAUDE.md; a thread can run on your computer through Remote Control, while a single task fits a cloud session and a scheduled job with no conversation fits a routine.

concepts.title: Desktop Code tab: Local, Cloud, SSH and WSL sessions
concepts.titleEs: Pestaña Code de Desktop: sesiones Local, Cloud, SSH y WSL
concepts.summary: Each Desktop Code session chooses an environment (Local, Cloud, SSH to a Linux or macOS host, or a WSL 2 distribution on Windows), a folder, a model and a permission mode (Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto, Bypass once enabled; dontAsk is CLI-only), with an optional worktree stored in .claude/worktrees/. Desktop shares CLAUDE.md, settings, hooks, skills and MCP files with the CLI; /desktop moves a CLI session into the app, /resume in Desktop picks up CLI sessions, and Continue in sends a local session to the cloud.

concepts.title: Preview servers in .claude/launch.json and autoVerify
concepts.titleEs: Servidores de preview en .claude/launch.json y autoVerify
concepts.summary: Desktop stores dev-server config in .claude/launch.json at the session folder root: a version plus a configurations array whose entries take name, runtimeExecutable with runtimeArgs (or program with args for a node script), port (default 3000), cwd, env (committed, so no secrets), autoPort and url. autoVerify is on by default so Claude screenshots and checks its changes in the Browser pane after edits; set "autoVerify": false at the top level to turn it off.

concepts.title: VS Code extension vs the CLI
concepts.titleEs: Extensión de VS Code vs la CLI
concepts.summary: The VS Code extension bundles a private copy of the CLI for its chat panel and does not put claude on your PATH, so running claude in the integrated terminal needs the standalone install; the two share conversation history (claude --resume) and ~/.claude/settings.json, while extension settings such as initialPermissionMode (read only from user settings), useTerminal and allowDangerouslySkipPermissions live in VS Code. Some CLI features (! bash shortcut, tab completion, all commands) are CLI-only, and the Web tab of Session history resumes cloud sessions as a local copy.

concepts.title: JetBrains plugin, /ide and the built-in ide MCP server
concepts.titleEs: Plugin de JetBrains, /ide y el servidor MCP ide integrado
concepts.summary: The JetBrains plugin bundles no CLI: it runs the claude you installed in the IDE terminal (set a custom Claude command if not on PATH), and /ide connects a session from an external terminal; Diff tool in /config (diffTool auto or terminal) chooses where diffs open. Both IDEs run a hidden local MCP server named ide that shares your selection and active file and exposes mcp__ide__getDiagnostics (plus mcp__ide__executeCode for Jupyter in VS Code); a Read deny rule keeps a file like .env out of that context.

concepts.title: Claude in Chrome vs computer use: which tool reaches the GUI
concepts.titleEs: Claude en Chrome vs computer use: qué herramienta llega a la interfaz
concepts.summary: Claude tries tools in this order: an MCP server for the service, then Bash, then Claude in Chrome for browser work, and only then computer use for native apps and simulators. Chrome is enabled per session with claude --chrome or by default from /chrome, uses your browser's login state and needs a /login claude.ai account; computer use is the built-in computer-use MCP server enabled in /mcp (macOS in the CLI, Pro/Max, interactive only), approved per app per session, locked to one session at a time and aborted with Esc.

concepts.title: Artifacts: publish session output as a live page
concepts.titleEs: Artifacts: publicar la salida de la sesión como página viva
concepts.summary: An artifact is a single self-contained HTML or Markdown page (no backend, 16 MiB max, strict CSP) that Claude publishes to a private claude.ai URL, republishes in place as versions, and you share from the page's Share control; /artifacts lists and attaches existing ones and Ctrl+] reopens the latest. It needs a /login claude.ai session on the Anthropic API, and you turn it off with "enableArtifact": false, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT=1 or Artifact in permissions.deny.

concepts.title: Voice dictation: /voice hold vs tap
concepts.titleEs: Dictado por voz: /voice hold vs tap
concepts.summary: /voice toggles dictation (/voice hold, /voice tap, /voice off) and persists as the voice object in user settings with enabled, mode and autoSubmit; hold mode records while Space is held, tap mode starts and sends with single taps and auto-submits transcripts of three or more words. It streams audio to Anthropic, needs a claude.ai account and a local microphone (not cloud or SSH sessions), follows the language setting, and is rebound via voice:pushToTalk in the Chat context of ~/.claude/keybindings.json.

concepts.title: Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS switches
concepts.titleEs: Interruptores de Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry y Claude Platform on AWS
concepts.summary: Each provider is switched on by its variable: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 (region from AWS_REGION, then AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, then the profile's region, then us-east-1), CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 with CLOUD_ML_REGION and ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1 with ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE, and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1 with the required ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID. Pin models for multi-user rollouts with ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, _SONNET_MODEL and _HAIKU_MODEL, and expect /logout and claude.ai-only features to be unavailable.

concepts.title: LLM gateway vs corporate proxy, and who gets billed
concepts.titleEs: LLM gateway vs proxy corporativo, y a quién se le cobra
concepts.summary: A corporate proxy (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY; no SOCKS; custom CA via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) sits in front of every server Claude Code talks to, while an LLM gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus a gateway credential such as ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or the built-in Claude apps gateway signed in with /login) centralizes provider credentials, budgets, usage tracking and audit. A gateway credential replaces the claude.ai subscription and bills the gateway's provider account, but ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL alone keeps the subscription login; put network variables in the settings env block so background agents get them, and check routing with /status.

concepts.title: Which features need a claude.ai subscription or a given plan
concepts.titleEs: Qué funciones requieren suscripción claude.ai o cierto plan
concepts.summary: The CLI, Agent SDK, IDE extensions, subagents, hooks, skills, CLAUDE.md, plugins, MCP, checkpoints and sandboxing work on every provider, but cloud sessions, mobile, Slack, Desktop, routines, ultrareview, Remote Control, Chrome, computer use, artifacts and voice need a claude.ai login. By plan, Code Review, server-managed settings and SSO are Team/Enterprise, computer use and Dispatch are Pro/Max only, and Remote Control is admin-enabled on Team/Enterprise; admins decide in order: API provider, how settings reach devices, what to enforce, usage visibility, data handling.

concepts.title: Self-hosted environments: cloud sessions on your own runners
concepts.titleEs: Entornos self-hosted: sesiones cloud en tus propios runners
concepts.summary: A self-hosted environment (Team/Enterprise beta, off until an Owner turns on Allow self-hosted environments) lets the same cloud-session UX execute on runners inside your network: an environment groups runners, a runner polls api.anthropic.com over outbound HTTPS, clones the repo and runs each session with your tooling and git credentials. Checkouts and artifacts stay on your hosts, but the conversation still goes to the Anthropic API for inference, which cannot be routed through Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry or an LLM gateway; to drive your own always-on machine instead, use Remote Control.

confusableGroups.title: Extension map vs guidance-vs-enforcement vs output styles
discriminators: loop-extension-map: the question is which feature fits a recurring trigger (repeated prompt, external data, flooding side task, second repo).
loop-guidance-vs-enforcement: the rule must hold every time no matter what Claude decides, so it needs a hook or permission rule, not an instruction.
model-output-styles: the change is about the shape of every response (length, tone, role, explanations), switchable with /output-style.

confusableGroups.title: Esc / queued Enter vs ! shell mode vs /btw
discriminators: interactive-interrupt-queue: you want to stop (Esc) or redirect (type + Enter) what Claude is doing in this turn.
interactive-input-prefixes: you want to run a command yourself with ! and put its output in context, or point at a file with @.
cmd-btw: you want a quick answer from what Claude already knows, with no tools and nothing added to history.

confusableGroups.title: Edit/Write vs Bash file changes vs rewind vs git
discriminators: tools-edit-vs-write: the change was made by Claude's file-editing tools (exact replacement or full overwrite), so it is checkpointed.
tools-bash-behavior: the change came from a shell command in a separate process; env vars do not persist and the file change is not checkpointed.
checkpoint-rewind-options: you need to pick which restore or summarize action to take from /rewind.
checkpoint-limits: the thing to undo was done via Bash, a background subagent, outside the session, a symlink or a remote system, so reach for git.

confusableGroups.title: Switching model vs changing effort or fast mode
discriminators: model-select: you want a different model (alias, pinned name, opusplan) or a second model consulted via the advisor.
model-effort-fast: you keep the model but change how much it reasons (effort, ultrathink) or its latency at higher cost (fast mode).

confusableGroups.title: Everyday commands vs inspection commands vs clean-config bisecting
discriminators: cmd-everyday-commands: you want to create or change something (/init a CLAUDE.md, /config a key, /add-dir, /diff, /export).
debug-inspect-commands: you want to see what is loaded or active (/context, /status, /doctor, /debug).
debug-clean-config: you suspect your customizations themselves and need to rule them out with --safe-mode or an empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

confusableGroups.title: Verify vs explore-plan-code vs failure-pattern fixes
discriminators: workflow-verify: the risk is Claude declaring done without proof; add a runnable check or a /goal, Stop hook or verifier.
workflow-explore-plan-code: the risk is solving the wrong problem; explore and plan in plan mode before editing.
workflow-failure-patterns: the session is already derailing (polluted context, repeated corrections); /clear, reprompt or delegate.

confusableGroups.title: /context vs /usage
discriminators: ctx-context-command: 'what is filling my window right now / did my CLAUDE.md load' → /context grid and Memory files list
cost-usage-command: 'how much did this session cost, is my cache hitting, what counts against my plan' → /usage (/cost, /stats)

confusableGroups.title: /clear vs /compact
discriminators: ctx-clear: switching to unrelated work or context polluted by failed attempts; you want nothing carried over, at zero cost
ctx-compact: same task continues but the window is full; you want a summary carried forward (optionally focused, or partial via /rewind)

confusableGroups.title: CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md vs auto memory vs .claude/rules/
discriminators: mem-claude-md-locations: you write it; facts needed in every session (build commands, conventions), scoped managed/user/project/local
mem-agents-md: the repo already has instructions for other coding agents; read only when no CLAUDE.md exists unless Project instructions says otherwise
mem-auto-memory: Claude writes it from your corrections and preferences; 'remember that...'; lives in ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/
mem-rules-paths: topic files in .claude/rules/, optionally gated by `paths` globs so they load only when matching files are read

confusableGroups.title: Cache invalidated vs cache expired
discriminators: cache-invalidators: the slow turn came right after you changed something in the prefix (model, effort, MCP servers, plugins, compaction)
cache-ttl: nothing changed but you were idle longer than the TTL (5m or 1h), so the first turn back recomputes everything

confusableGroups.title: --continue vs --resume vs /branch
discriminators: session-continue: 'pick up the last conversation in this directory', no choice needed
session-resume: you need a specific older session (picker, name, ID, PR) or a -p session by ID
session-branch: you want a copy to explore an alternative while keeping the original conversation intact

confusableGroups.title: claudeMdExcludes vs Read deny vs sparsePaths vs --add-dir/additionalDirectories
discriminators: large-scope-instructions: other teams' instructions pollute context → choose the launch directory and use claudeMdExcludes
large-reduce-reads: Claude opens generated/vendored files or checks out too much → Read deny rules, code intelligence, worktree.sparsePaths
large-add-dir: Claude needs access to a sibling package or repo → --add-dir (loads skills) vs additionalDirectories (access only)

confusableGroups.title: Which file reaches whom vs why a committed key is ignored
discriminators: settings-scopes-files: the question is who a setting should affect (me everywhere, the team, me in this repo, the whole org)
settings-repo-file-limits: the key is already in .claude/settings.json but a teammate doesn't get it (ignored Scope or waiting for workspace trust)

confusableGroups.title: Settings levels vs one-session overrides vs the env block
discriminators: settings-precedence-order: the same key sits in several settings files; the highest level (managed > CLI > local > project > user) wins
settings-session-overrides: you want a value for this run only, via --settings, a flag like --model, or a paired env var decided per key
settings-env-block: you want an environment variable applied on every launch from a settings file; it overwrites the shell export

confusableGroups.title: Permission rules vs auto-mode classifier vs sandbox vs instructions
discriminators: perm-rule-eval-order: tool-pattern allow/ask/deny checked before any tool runs, in every mode; deny > ask > allow
auto-mode-classifier: a second model that reviews only the actions rules didn't resolve, and only in auto mode
sandbox-bash-basics: the OS enforces file and network limits on the running shell process, regardless of what the command string looked like
security-enforcement-layers: CLAUDE.md or prompt text only steers the model; it is never an enforced boundary

confusableGroups.title: dontAsk / bypassPermissions vs an isolation boundary
discriminators: mode-bypass-vs-dontask: deciding whether tool calls run without a prompt (deny everything unlisted vs skip all checks)
sandbox-environments-choice: deciding what a run can reach once it executes (Bash sandbox, sandbox runtime, dev container, VM, cloud)

confusableGroups.title: autoMode rules vs permission-rule checkpoints
discriminators: auto-mode-environment: prose entries read by the classifier (environment, allow, soft_deny, hard_deny) to stop false positives or add org-specific blocks
auto-mode-checkpoints: you want a guaranteed prompt or hard block for a specific command, via permissions.ask or permissions.deny, which run before the classifier

confusableGroups.title: Permission-rule paths vs sandbox paths
discriminators: perm-read-edit-paths: inside Read(...)/Edit(...) rules, //path is absolute and /path is relative to the settings source
sandbox-config-keys: inside sandbox.filesystem arrays, /path is absolute and ./path is the project root (or ~/.claude in user settings)

confusableGroups.title: How managed policy arrives vs what it locks
discriminators: managed-delivery: the channel and file location (claude.ai console, MDM/registry, managed-settings.json) and which source wins
managed-only-locks: the keys that restrict what lower levels may add (allowManaged*Only, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh)

confusableGroups.title: Standard data policy vs Zero Data Retention
discriminators: security-data-usage: default training and retention by account type, local transcripts and telemetry opt-outs
security-zdr: an Enterprise org-level agreement where Anthropic stores no prompts/responses and data-storing features are disabled

confusableGroups.title: Skill vs CLAUDE.md vs hook/subagent vs context: fork
discriminators: skill-vs-claudemd: the question is always-on facts vs on-demand reference or a /name workflow
skill-vs-hook-subagent: the question is guaranteed enforcement (hook) or isolated context returning a summary (subagent) vs instructions Claude interprets
skill-context-fork: a skill's own content becomes a fresh subagent's task via context: fork + agent, with no conversation history

confusableGroups.title: disable-model-invocation vs user-invocable: false vs skillOverrides vs paths
discriminators: skill-disable-model-invocation: only YOU may run it (side effects like deploy); description leaves context
skill-user-invocable-false: only CLAUDE may run it (background knowledge); hidden from the / menu
skill-visibility-overrides: you can't or won't edit SKILL.md, so you set visibility from settings (on/name-only/user-invocable-only/off) or gate it with Skill() rules
skill-paths: auto-load only when Claude works on files matching globs

confusableGroups.title: $ARGUMENTS/$N vs !`command` vs ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}
discriminators: skill-arguments: the value comes from what the user typed after /name
skill-dynamic-context: the value comes from running a shell command before Claude reads the skill
skill-env-substitutions: the value is a Claude Code path or session fact (skill dir, project dir, session ID, effort)

confusableGroups.title: Skill location vs command file vs name collision
discriminators: skill-locations: the question is which sessions load a skill (personal, project, nested, plugin, claude.ai)
skill-commands-merged: the question is .claude/commands/x.md vs .claude/skills/x/SKILL.md format
skill-name-resolution: two sources define the same name and you must say which one /name runs

confusableGroups.title: What persists: skill content vs allowed-tools grant vs supporting files
discriminators: skill-content-lifecycle: the rendered SKILL.md stays in context across turns and is re-attached after compaction
skill-allowed-tools: the tool grant lasts only for the invoking turn and clears on your next message
skill-supporting-files: extra files load only when Claude chooses to read them; scripts are executed, never loaded

confusableGroups.title: Built-in command vs bundled skills (/batch, /simplify, /code-review, /run, /verify)
discriminators: skill-bundled-vs-builtin: prompt-based (Claude orchestrates) vs fixed CLI logic like /compact
skill-bundled-catalog: large parallel migration (/batch), cleanup (/simplify), bug review (/code-review), debug log (/debug), repeat (/loop)
skill-run-verify: confirm a change in the running app rather than via tests, optionally with a recorded launch recipe

confusableGroups.title: Hook guarantee vs additionalContext vs CLAUDE.md
discriminators: hook-deterministic-control: the action must always or never happen regardless of what Claude decides -> a hook (or permission rule), not CLAUDE.md guidance
hook-decision-additional-context: Claude needs a changing fact at a specific moment (branch, CI result, which test command) -> additionalContext from a hook; static conventions stay in CLAUDE.md

confusableGroups.title: SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit vs PreToolUse vs PostToolUse vs Stop
discriminators: hook-event-lifecycle-order: once per session or per prompt (load context at start, validate the prompt, clean up at end) -> SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd
hook-event-pretooluse-vs-posttooluse: around each tool call -> PreToolUse to block or rewrite before it runs, PostToolUse to react after it succeeded
hook-event-stop: when Claude is about to finish its response and you want to verify or keep it working -> Stop (SubagentStop for subagents, StopFailure for API errors)

confusableGroups.title: matcher vs if
discriminators: hook-config-matcher: filters the matcher group by the event's field (tool name, session source, notification type); exact list or regex string
hook-config-if: filters one handler by tool name AND arguments using permission-rule syntax like Bash(git *); tool events only

confusableGroups.title: Exit codes vs JSON output
discriminators: hook-io-exit-codes: just block or stay silent -> exit 2 with a stderr message (exit 1 does NOT block)
hook-io-json-output: need allow/ask, rewritten input, context, a user warning or stopping Claude -> exit 0 and print a JSON object

confusableGroups.title: PreToolUse permissionDecision vs PermissionRequest decision
discriminators: hook-decision-pretooluse: runs on every matching tool call before permission checks, in every mode including -p; hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow/deny/ask/defer
hook-decision-permissionrequest: runs only when a permission prompt is about to appear; hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior allow/deny, can set mode via updatedPermissions; exit 2 ignored

confusableGroups.title: command vs http/mcp_tool vs prompt/agent hooks
discriminators: hook-type-command: a deterministic local script; the default, supports async and exit codes
hook-type-http-mcp: the logic lives in a web service (POST) or an MCP server tool; block only via a JSON body
hook-type-prompt-agent: the decision needs judgment; a model returns {ok, reason}, agent when it must read files or run tests

confusableGroups.title: Why a hook does not run: trust vs disabled vs misconfigured
discriminators: hook-safety-trust: interactive session in a folder whose workspace trust dialog was not accepted -> settings hooks are held back
hook-safety-disable: disableAllHooks is true at the winning settings level, or allowManagedHooksOnly blocks non-managed hooks
hook-debug-diagnose: hook is missing from /hooks or listed but not firing -> wrong file, matcher array, wrong case, or JSON the parser ignores

confusableGroups.title: Subagents vs agent view vs agent teams vs workflows vs cross-session messaging
discriminators: subagent-when-to-use: Claude delegates a side task inside one conversation and gets a summary back
agentview-dispatch: YOU hand off independent tasks as background sessions and check back later
team-vs-subagents: a lead spawns teammates that must talk to each other and share a task list
workflow-when-to-use: a script, not Claude's turn-by-turn judgment, orchestrates dozens to hundreds of agents
crosssession-messaging: sessions you already run yourself need to pass a finding or status to each other

confusableGroups.title: Forked subagent (/subtask) vs copy session (/fork) vs move to background (/bg)
discriminators: subagent-fork: a subagent inside this session with the full conversation; only its result comes back to you
agentview-bg-vs-fork: a whole separate background session, either moved (/bg) or copied (/fork), that you manage from agent view

confusableGroups.title: Which subagent file wins vs which model a subagent runs on
discriminators: subagent-scope-precedence: two definitions share a name: managed > --agents > .claude/agents > ~/.claude/agents > plugin
subagent-model-order: which model runs: per-invocation model > frontmatter model > CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL > main model

confusableGroups.title: --worktree vs .worktreeinclude vs WorktreeCreate hook
discriminators: worktree-flag: start a session in an isolated git checkout under .claude/worktrees/<name>
worktree-include: the worktree is missing gitignored files like .env
worktree-nongit-hooks: the repo isn't git, or worktrees must be created somewhere custom

confusableGroups.title: /loop vs /goal vs channels
discriminators: loop-scheduled-tasks: the next turn starts when a time interval elapses (polling, reminders)
goal-condition: the next turn starts when the previous one ends, until an evaluator confirms a condition
channels-push-events: the next turn starts when an external system pushes an event into the open session

confusableGroups.title: HTTP vs stdio MCP transport
discriminators: mcp-transport-http: the server is a hosted URL (Notion, Sentry, a remote API) and may need OAuth or a header; SSE is its deprecated predecessor
mcp-transport-stdio: Claude Code spawns a local command (npx, python, a binary) with `--` before its args and `--env` for its variables

confusableGroups.title: MCP local vs project vs user scope, and plugin install scopes
discriminators: mcp-scope-local: only me, only this project, stored in ~/.claude.json under the project path; the default
mcp-scope-project: the whole team via a committed .mcp.json at the repo root, with an approval prompt
mcp-scope-user: only me but every project, top-level mcpServers in ~/.claude.json
plugin-install-scopes: it's a plugin, not an MCP server, so the scope writes enabledPlugins into ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json

confusableGroups.title: managed-mcp.json / managedMcpServers vs allow/deny lists
discriminators: mcp-managed-mcp-json: the organization defines the servers themselves, either exclusively (managed-mcp.json) or in addition to users' own (managedMcpServers)
mcp-allow-deny-lists: users still add servers and policy filters which of them may load by URL, command or name

confusableGroups.title: Plugin layout vs plugin.json vs marketplace.json
discriminators: plugin-layout: where component files sit (skills/, agents/, hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json at the plugin root, not inside .claude-plugin/)
plugin-manifest: .claude-plugin/plugin.json describes ONE plugin: name, version, userConfig, dependencies
plugin-marketplace-json: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lists MANY plugins with name + source and an owner

confusableGroups.title: Plugin version field vs dependency version range
discriminators: plugin-versioning-updates: when do users of MY plugin get a new copy (version field, commit SHA, auto-update)
plugin-dependencies: which version of ANOTHER plugin mine needs (semver range resolved against <name>--v<version> tags)

confusableGroups.title: claude plugin validate vs eval vs details
discriminators: plugin-dev-loop: does it load? validate checks files and schema, --plugin-dir and /reload-plugins iterate, the Errors tab explains failures
plugin-eval: does it change Claude's behavior for the better? graded cases vs a no-plugin baseline, costs model calls
plugin-details-cost: what does it cost every session? inventory and Always-on tokens

confusableGroups.title: --bare vs settingSources vs system prompt choice vs tenant isolation
discriminators: headless-bare-mode: a CLI `claude -p` run that must skip hooks, skills, MCP, plugins, auto memory and CLAUDE.md
sdk-setting-sources: an SDK `query()` choosing which of user/project/local filesystem config loads
sdk-system-prompt: deciding the base instructions (minimal, `claude_code` preset, `append`, custom), not which files load
sdk-secure-deployment: tenants sharing a container, where `settingSources: []` alone is not enough (auto memory, config dir, cwd)

confusableGroups.title: CLI unattended flags vs SDK permission flow/canUseTool vs hook callbacks
discriminators: headless-unattended-permissions: CLI flags on `claude -p` (`--allowedTools`, `--permission-mode`, `--permission-prompts none`)
sdk-permission-flow: the fixed check order in the SDK and the last-resort `canUseTool` callback that asks a human
sdk-hooks-callbacks: code that runs first on every matching call and can deny, rewrite or defer it

confusableGroups.title: Output formats vs structured output vs ResultMessage
discriminators: output-formats-json-stream: how the CLI prints the run (`text`, `json`, `stream-json`)
output-json-schema: you need data matching your schema in `structured_output`
sdk-loop-results: in SDK code, the final message whose `subtype` says success or which limit was hit

confusableGroups.title: Custom tool vs external MCP server vs subagent in the SDK
discriminators: sdk-custom-tools: your own function in application code, served in-process by `createSdkMcpServer`
sdk-mcp-servers: an existing server you start by command (stdio) or reach by URL (http/sse)
sdk-subagents: delegating a whole subtask to a separate agent with its own prompt, tools and context

confusableGroups.title: Resume/fork vs file rewind vs SessionStore hosting
discriminators: sdk-sessions: return to or branch the conversation history on the same machine
sdk-file-checkpointing: undo file changes on disk while the conversation stays
sdk-hosting-patterns: containers that die or scale, so transcripts must move to a `SessionStore`

confusableGroups.title: In-stream cost fields vs OpenTelemetry export
discriminators: sdk-cost-tracking: read `total_cost_usd` / `modelUsage` from the result message in your own code
sdk-observability: ship metrics, logs and traces to an OTLP backend for dashboards across runs

confusableGroups.title: Raw claude -p vs Agent SDK vs GitHub Action vs GitLab job
discriminators: headless-print-basics: a shell script or npm script calling `claude -p` directly
sdk-vs-other-tools: an application in Python/TypeScript that needs typed messages and callbacks
gha-setup-auth: getting the GitHub App, secret and workflow file in place
gha-modes-and-args: deciding `@claude` mentions vs a `prompt`-driven run and passing `claude_args`
gitlab-ci-job: the pipeline lives in `.gitlab-ci.yml` and changes arrive as MRs

confusableGroups.title: Cloud session vs --cloud/--teleport handoff vs Remote Control vs Project vs self-hosted environment
discriminators: cloud-session-basics: the task should run on an Anthropic VM from a fresh GitHub clone and keep going with your laptop closed
cloud-handoff-flags: you are moving work between terminal and cloud; --cloud starts a new cloud session, --teleport pulls one down with its branch
rc-remote-control: the session stays on your machine with local files and MCP servers, and your phone or browser is just a window into it
projects-coordinator: a stream of related tasks where Claude itself starts and tracks many threads from one conversation
ent-self-hosted-environments: the organization needs cloud sessions to execute on its own runners inside its network

confusableGroups.title: Routine triggers vs Desktop scheduled task vs Auto-fix
discriminators: routine-triggers: unattended cloud work on a schedule (1 h minimum), an HTTP /fire call or a GitHub pull_request/release event
routine-desktop-scheduled-tasks: recurring work that needs local files and can run every minute, but only while your computer is awake and the app open
cloud-autofix-pr: one existing PR should be watched and fixed as CI fails or reviewers comment

confusableGroups.title: Managed Code Review vs /code-review and ultrareview vs security plugins
discriminators: review-managed-code-review: automatic inline comments on GitHub PRs for a Team/Enterprise org, tuned with REVIEW.md and @claude review
review-local-vs-ultra: you ask for a review from your session, locally (/code-review) or as a deep verified cloud pass before merging (/code-review ultra, claude ultrareview)
review-security-plugins: security-specific checks, either automatic while Claude writes (security-guidance) or an on-demand vulnerability scan with patches (/claude-security)

confusableGroups.title: VS Code extension vs JetBrains plugin
discriminators: ide-vscode-extension: a graphical chat panel with its own bundled CLI; claude is not on PATH until you install the standalone CLI
ide-jetbrains-plugin: no bundled CLI; the plugin runs your installed claude in the IDE terminal, and /ide connects external terminals

confusableGroups.title: Cloud provider switch vs LLM gateway vs corporate proxy
discriminators: provider-cloud-env-vars: inference and billing go directly to your AWS, GCP or Azure account via a CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* variable

provider-gateway-vs-proxy: traffic goes through infrastructure your org runs, either a gateway at ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL that swaps credentials and tracks usage, or an HTTPS_PROXY that only forwards and inspects
